The Amendment was the constitutional embodiment of the people’s collective demand for electoral integrity, and hence, a legitimate expression of popular sovereignty under Article 7.

170. On that score, maintaining the stringent and narrow parameters of review, it is earnestly hoped that the Thirteenth Amendment, in all its legislative wisdom, shall be recognized as a remarkable and awe-inspiring constitutional achievement, designed to uphold the people’s sovereign will—to exercise their right of franchise freely, fairly, and impartially. In truth, the non-party caretaker system did not erode but rather fortified the basic structure of the Constitution by ensuring the sanctity of Article 7, the pole star of the Republic, wherein sovereignty belongs to the people.

171. Therefore, the majority view, in seeking to locate democracy only in the continuous operation of political government, ignored the deeper constitutional wisdom—that when the process of governance fails to reflect the people’s free will, it is the Constitution’s duty to restore that will by any legitimate means. The 13th Amendment, thus, was not a rupture but a reaffirmation of the constitutional continuum, perfectly consistent with the intent of the framers who envisioned democracy not as a privilege of politicians, but as a right of the governed.

172. The majority judgment, in striking down a people-empowered reform, inadvertently weakened the very edifice it sought to defend. The Constitution, being a living document, demands interpretive flexibility anchored in public sovereignty, not rigidity imposed by judicial abstraction. In these circumstances, the review of the 13th Amendment judgment is not only warranted but imperative—to realign constitutional interpretation with its foundational spirit. The restoration of the caretaker system, or at least the reaffirmation of its constitutional legitimacy, would vindicate the framers’ vision, reinforce people’s supremacy under Article 7, and revive the moral and institutional integrity of democracy in Bangladesh.

173. All arguments placed before this Court by the learned counsels from every side including those advanced by the interveners have been carefully heard and appreciated. The citations from national and international jurisdictions—as cited by them have also been meticulously considered from a comparative perspective.

174. Comparative understanding from Marbury v. Madison (1803) 2 L.ED.60, A.K. Gopalan V. State of Madras AIR 1950 SC 27, State v. Dosso 11 DLR (1959) 1, Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan AIR 1965 SC 845, Golak Nath v. State of Punjab AIR 1967 SC 1643, Asma Jilani v. Government of Punjab PLD1972(SC)139, and Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala AIR 1973 SC 1461, Begum Nusrat Bhutto V. Chief of Army Staff and Federation of Pakistan, PLD 1977 SC 657 and Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India AIR 1978 SC 597 and from our jurisdiction the most celebrated decision of Anwar Hossain Chowdhury v. Bangladesh (8th Amendment Case) 41 DLR AD 165 demonstrates that Constitutional orders sometimes admit limited adaptation to sustain the higher values of democracy and rule of law. The jurisprudence developed through the 8th Amendment Case in Bangladesh and the comparative decisions abroad consistently emphasise that continuity of democratic governance is a Constitutional imperative. Even during interruptions or exceptional arrangements, the legitimacy of the Republic must rest upon the will of the people. It is further added that in the said case, Badrul Haider Chowdhury, J delineated 21 basic features of the Constitution which I think has not at all disregarded in any manner by the Thirteenth Amendment. The said Amendment, was an indigenous adaptation within our own Constitutional frame, a Constitutional device born of necessity but grounded in legitimacy.

175. The long march of constitutional jurisprudence, from Marbury v. Madison to Maneka Gandhi teaches that constitutions live not by their letters alone but by the spirit they breathe. In Marbury, Chief Justice Marshall proclaimed that it is the “province and duty of the judicial department to say what the law is,” thereby affirming the judiciary’s solemn responsibility to uphold the Constitution above transient majorities. In contrast, the narrow literalism of A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras—which treated fundamental rights as isolated compartments—served as a reminder that rigidity in interpretation may defeat the very liberty it seeks to preserve. Its later correction in Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, which harmonized rights and emphasized due process as the essence of fairness, reestablished the Constitution as a living, organic covenant between the State and the people. These lessons find renewed relevance in the present review, for the Thirteenth Amendment, conceived to secure free and fair elections, must be judged not by its procedural novelty but by its constitutional purpose—to uphold democracy, restore public faith, and give life to the people’s sovereignty enshrined in Article 7, the polestar of our constitutional order.

176. In Anwar Hossain Chowdhury v. Bangladesh (8th Amendment Case, 41 DLR (AD) 165), the Appellate Division, speaking through Chief Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed, firmly established the doctrine of basic structure as a constitutional safeguard against arbitrary or destructive amendments. The Court held that although Parliament possesses wide authority under Article 142 to amend the Constitution, such power is not absolute—it cannot alter or destroy the core identity of the Constitution. The judges identified a set of foundational principles that constitute this inviolable framework, including the supremacy of the Constitution, the sovereignty of the people as declared in Article 7, and the republican and democratic character of the State. It further emphasized the unitary nature of the

177. Republic, the rule of law, the separation of powers, and above all, the independence of the judiciary, as essential features ensuring the balance among the three organs of the State. The parliamentary system of government, based on collective responsibility of the Cabinet to the Jatiya Sangsad, and the power of judicial review were also recognized as inherent to the constitutional order. Alongside these, the Court viewed fundamental rights, equality before law, and freedom of expression as indispensable attributes of constitutional democracy.

178. The luminous grandeur of Article 7 of the Constitution of Bangladesh solemnly enshrines the principle of the inviolability of the Constitution, proclaiming: “All powers in the Republic belong to the people, and their exercise on behalf of the people shall be effected only under, and by the authority of, this Constitution.”

179. In its magnanimity, Article 7 affirms the democratic ethos of Bangladesh, ensuring that the sovereignty of the people remains unassailable and that no usurpation or extra-constitutional authority can compromise the will of the nation. Its gloriousness lies not merely in its words, but in its enduring assurance that the sanctity of constitutional governance is both supreme and immutable, offering a beacon of stability and legality through times of political turbulence.

180. The distinguished constitutionalist and the Senior Advocate, Mr. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed, in his celebrated submissions in the 8th Amendment Case, illuminated this principle with his exceptional clarity and eloquence. With his characteristic grace, he drew attention to the profound beauty and structural harmony of our Constitution, observing that it stands unparalleled among modern constitutions. He especially emphasized that Article 7—rising at the very threshold of the Constitution like a Statue of Liberty, proclaiming the sovereignty of the people—is a unique and incomparable feature not to be found in any other constitution.

181. The doctrine of necessity, when evaluated in terms of Article 7 of our Constitution—the polestar declaring that all power belongs to the people—receives its legitimacy from the Constitution itself. It is a doctrine of preservation, not of usurpation. When the ordinary political process fails to secure the people’s right to franchise, the Constitution may legitimately bend to save itself from breaking. The caretaker arrangement was such a measured bending—temporary, proportionate, and aimed solely at restoring democratic trust.

182. In the light of the foregoing discussion, I find that the discrepancy between the short order and the full judgment constitutes an error apparent on the record; that the Thirteenth Amendment was enacted in good faith within the Constitutional mandate of Article 7; that the doctrine of necessity, properly invoked, legitimized the caretaker arrangement as a temporary safeguard of democracy; and that the basic structure of the Constitution was not at all destroyed but preserved by that arrangement.

183. The Constitution is not a rigid parchment; it is a living covenant between the State and its people. It endures when it listens to the people’s conscience. The Thirteenth Amendment, born of that conscience, remains a symbol of the Republic’s capacity to renew its democratic faith.

184. The people’s will governs all other yardsticks of the nation. It is the cumulative voice of the citizens which, time and again, through the labyrinth of history, has moulded the substratum of our Republic. This is the essence of the Article 7. This provision is unique by itself as it cannot be found in any other Constitution. When the people’s will is preserved, the Constitution breathes; when it is denied, it withers.

185. To conclude my part, it is fitting to return to the timeless wisdom that has guided constitutional thought across centuries. In this spirit, I may appropriately echo the resounding voice of Aristotle, whose insight continues to illuminate the path of constitutionalism through the ages: "To live by the rule of the Constitution ought not to be regarded as slavery, but rather as salvation". (Aristotle's Politics (335–322 BC), pp. 233–34)

186. Accordingly, I concur in holding that this Civil Appeal alongwith the review petitions succeed and accordingly the same is allowed.

187. The short order dated 20.11.2025 reads thus: “By a unanimous decision, the civil appeals are allowed and civil review petitions are disposed of accordingly.

188. This Court is satisfied that the judgment under review is tainted by several cited errors apparent on the face of the record.

189. It follows that the judgment under review, is, hereby, set aside in its entirety.

190. Consequently, the provisions of Chapter IIA of Part IV of the Constitution relating to the Non-Party Care-taker Government (NPCG) as inserted by section 3 of the Constitution (Thirteenth Amendment) Act, 1996 (Act No. 1 of 1996), are found to have hereby been activated and revived upon this Court's ruling as above.

191. Such revival, though ensures automatic restoration of Chapter IIA containing NPCG provisions, its operation, however, is subject to the enforcement of the provisions of the revived Articles 58B(1) and 58C(2) of the Constitution.

192. It follows, therefore, that the now restored and revived Chapter IIA NPCG provisions can operate only prospectively.

193. The Judgment in detail shall follow.”

The office is directed to communicate the order forthwith to the High Court Division.

End.

lawyer:
Shorful Islam Khan, Advocate-----For the Petitioner.

parties:
Sadia Chowdhury Parag ----- Petitioner 
Vs.
Chairman, Film Censor Board & ors ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
MA Aziz J: This Rule was issued calling upon respondent No. 1 only i.e. the Chairman, Film Censor Board, to show cause, why the certificate issued by him for release/exhibition of the film 'Hason Raja' should not be suspended till hearing of the Rule as prayed for. Release of the film was stayed for 4 (four) weeks by order dated 14-12-2002.

2. On a reference to the prayer we have noticed a very unusual and curious phenomenon i.e. prayer (A) was couched/made in the manner as follows:

"A) Issue a Rule Nisi calling upon respondent No. 1 to show cause, why the certificate  issued by him for exhibition of the film "Hason Raja" should not be suspended till hearing of the Rule:

B)	Direct respondent No. 1 to certify and transmit the records and other relevant documents to this Hon'ble Court for their perusal by their Lordships:

C)	Restrain by an order of injunction the respondent No. 3 from releasing and exhibiting the film 'Hason Raja' pending hearing of the Rule.

D)	Make the Rule absolute.

E)	Pass such other or further order or orders as to your Lordships may deem fit and proper."

3. Having gone through the prayer and having heard the submissions of Mr Shorful Islam Khan, learned Counsel for the petitioner who urged upon the court to dispose of the Rule instead of making the same absolute, we are of opinion that even if the Rule is made absolute, it will serve no fruitful purpose for the petitioner because the prayer was not for issuing any Rule calling upon respondent No.1 to show cause, why the censorship certificate issued for screening the film 'Hason Raja' should not be declared to have been done without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect. Instead the prayer was couched in the following language as contained in prayer "A" referred to above.

4. Mr Khan argued his case very strenuously and tried to impress upon the Court that Dewan Hason Raja, the biggest Zaminder of Sylhet at the time, was a mystic poet and a saint. But the film belittled him by depicting him (the great grandfather of the petitioner) as a Womaniser, Don Juan, Philanderer and Casanova, which he was not. Hence, if such a distorted and untrue version of the saint is allowed to be screened, it will deeply hurt the religious sentiment of his followers who are countless and numerous in number and as such this sinister attempt/move must of necessity be nipped in the bud.

5. Mr Shorful Islam Khan having realised the infirmity and weakness of his case in his usual candidness asked the Court in the face of the prayer of Mrs Sigma Huda, learned Counsel for respondent No. 3 [Helal Khan, producer and actor (hero of the film)] demanding cost and damages for not being able to screen the film owing to the order of stay passed at the time of issuance of the rule on 14-12-2002, to dispose of the Rule and abandoned his prayer to make the Rule absolute without cost firstly, because the amount claimed by the producer is a staggering and colossal sum i.e. Taka 1 (one) million per day and secondly, because the petitioner, an impecunious great grand-daughter of Dewan Hason Raja genuinely felt aggrieved by the filming of the great saint as a sensual, hot-headed and hot- blooded Zamindar who having had vast wealth, power and influence gave vent to his relentless and unrestricted passion and lust for women and unbounded fondness and sense of attachment for professional dancer-cum-singer commonly known as Baizee (বাইজি) ।

6. The petitioner Mrs Sadia Chowdhury Porag in paragraph 3 of the Writ Petition stated that Hason Raja's ancestor Raja Birendra Chandra Singha Deb embraced Islam and adopted the name Babu Khan. Birendra's father having failed to persuade his son to renounce Islam, urged upon the Fouzdar of Sylhet to get Birendra (Babu Khan) married to a woman of respectable and decent origin and lineage. Babu Khan married Hurmat Jahan, daughter of a Muslim Quraish family of Teghoria. She inherited the Zamindary of her father at Rampasha in Sunamgonj. After the untimely death of his only brother Ubaydur Reza Chowdhury and the death of his father, Hason Raja inherited the Zamindaries of his father and mother comprising 3(three) hundred thousand big has of land and his huge wealth and power made Hason Raja an object of jealousy of the other Zamindars of Sylhet who kept on trying to tarnish the image of Hason Raja till he withdrew himself from worldly life. It is further stated that one Prithi Khan Chanda wrote a story depicting Hason Raja as a licentious, whimsical and capricious Zamindar to the great annoyance of the disciples of the great saint. This was protested by Professor Dewan Azraf, grandson of Hason Raja and father of the petitioner, which was published in a magazine called the Bichitra and the Producer Helal Khan borrowed that distorted and disparaging story as the theme of his film though Hason Raja led a puritan and pious life and that is the impression he left behind. But the film has demolished that impression.

7. It is submitted that Hason Raja had several wives of whom Asia Banu Chowdhury had only two daughters namely, Rowshan Jahan Banu and Rowshan Hasan Banu. He had no male child. Respondent No. 3 i.e. Helal Khan, in Lis film falsely projected Hason Raja to have had a son and that if the film is allowed to be screened with those distorted facts, the image of the saint would be seriously impaired. Mr Khan also quoted some assertions made in a paper called 'Jagobheri'. But we think that those assertions are not at all relevant for deciding the issues before us simply because in this case we are concerned with as to whether the film 'Hason Raja' has in any way tarnished and disparaged the good name, fame and image of Hason Raja.

8. The next submission of Mr Khan is that cinema being a very powerful medium has tremendous influence and effect upon the impressionist mind of the youths as well as the disciples of Hason Raja most of whom are people of simple and humble origin and background living in urban as well as rural areas where this powerful medium has reached and if the film "Hason Raja" is allowed to be screened it would have a devastating effect upon the countless disciples and admirers of Hason Raja because their religious feelings would be mortally wounded on watching their saint and Guru being depicted a wealthy and mighty Zamindar, with all the vices associated with Zamindari, specially the alleged outrageous sensuality of Hason Raza, his patronisation of the Baizees, so much so that his widowed mother Hurmat Jahan finding no other alternative had to appear at the 'Jalsha' in the guise of a Baizee to restrain and bring back her son Hason to the right track. This particular scene was taken exception to by Mr Shorful Islam Khan as obscene and objectionable and made a serious, sustained and sentimental exhortation that respondent No. 3 the hero (actor) and producer of the film managed the Film Censor Board and procured the necessary certificate from the said Board, that before issuing the certificate the Film Censor Board did not exercise due care, caution and circumspection or, in other words, there was a total non-application of mind in allowing the film to be released.

9. Mrs Sigma Huda, learned Counsel, filed power on behalf of respondent No. 3 although initially no Rule was prayed for and issued upon respondent No. 3. (Helal Khan, the actor and producer of the film). Rule was issued only upon respondent No. 1 i.e. the Chairman, Film Censor Board. Subsequently Rule was issued upon respondent No. 3 and he contested the same by filing an affidavit-in-opposition denying all the allegations and assertions made in the Writ Petition, contending, inter alia, that Hason Raja was not only a Zamindar, he was a mystic poet, devoted singer, a philosopher and an ascetic. His life was a varied and colourful one. He was supremely successful both in spiritual and secular life. He had an immeasurable and unquenchable thirst for unification with the greater soul and the quest for the answer as to "Who am I? Where have I come from? And where shall I go," went on unabated. It is not easy to comprehend the inner truth of the life of Hason Raja and he was easily misunderstood by his contemporaries on seeing the plurality of manifestations of his ever-expanding horizon of life Petitioner's allegation that the film "Hason Raja" maliciously depicted the great saint and mystic poet as a Philanderer, Casanova and Don Juan has been emphatically denied and respondent No. 3 asserted that it is the petitioner herself who defamed, debased and lowered down Hason Raja in her book called "প্রেম বাজারে হাছন রাজা" published in 1995. "মরমী কবি দেওয়ান হাছন রাজার নারী সঙ্গপ্রিয়তা দোষনীয় ছিল," which was discarded and condemned by no less a person than her father Professor Dewan Azraf, grandson of Hason Raja saying "একজন পুরুষ বা নারীর ধর্মই বিপরীত লিঙ্গের মানুষের প্রতি দুর্বল থাকা বা আকর্ষণ বোধ করা । ইসলাম ধর্ম মুলতঃ এ একারণে পুরুষের জন্য চারজন রমনী বৈধ করে দিয়েছে। আর নারীদের ক্ষেত্রে সে সুযোগ দিয়েছে একটু ঘুরিয়ে, স্বামী তালাকের মাধ্যমে।" Probhat Kumar Sharma evaluated Hason Raja in the following manner "বাঙলার সেই মধ্যযুগে এদেশে শিক্ষার বহুল প্রচার না হওয়ায় তাহার শিক্ষার প্রতি তখন কোন মনোযোগই দেওয়া হয় নাই। কিন্তু বনের ফুল যেমন মালীর হাতের সেবার অপেক্ষা না রাখিয়াই আপনার মত বর্ণে গন্ধে ভরিয়া উঠে, শিক্ষার অভাবের মধ্যেও তেমনি এই বাউল কবির চিত্ত বৈরাগ্য ও প্রেমের আলোকে এক রমণীর বন্য সন্দৌযে বিকশিত হইয়া উঠিয়াছিল । তাই বিকশিত হইলেও সেই বনফুলের মর্যাদা নগরের রাজোদ্যানে যে হয় নাই। তাহাতে বিস্মিত হইবার কোন কারন নাই। হাছন রাজা সাহেব যে সমাজ, যে রীতিনীতি, যে প্রকার আবেষ্টনের মধ্যে লালিত পালিত হইয়া উঠিয়াছিলেন বিংশ শতাব্দীর সমাজের সঙ্গে তাহার সুর মিলে না। কাজেই বিংশ শতাব্দীর সমাজ চিত্তের মাপকাঠি দ্বারা তাহার বিচার করিতে গেলে তাহার প্রতিভার অবিচার করা হইবে।"

10. Mrs Sigma Huda appearing for respondent No. 3 (Producer and actor Helal Khan) in her affidavit-in-opposition stated in paragraph 5 that the petitioner in her above named book edited by Dr Abul Ahshan Chowdhury had herself defamed, damaged and assassinated the character of Hasan Raja stating "জমিদার দেওয়ান হাসান রাজা যৌবনের বহু সুন্দরী রমনীর শয্যাসঙ্গী হয়ে সন্তান সন্ততি জন্মদান করেছিলেন। যে সমস্থ রমনীর সঙ্গে দেওয়ান হাসান রাজার ঔরসজাত সন্তান আগমন ও ভুমিস্ট লাভ হতো সেই সকল রমনীবৃন্দ প্রায় সকলেই কুমারী মাতা হয়ে আরাধ্য পুরুষ দেওয়ান হাসান রাজাকে ভালবেসে মন প্রান উজার করে জীবন তরিয়ে দিয়েছিলেন। এমনও দৃষ্টান্ত পাওয়া গিয়াছে যে, কোন কোন কন্যা কুমারীর রচিত শয্যায় হয়ত তিনি বছর খানেক কিংবা মাস ছয়েক সঙ্গ দিয়েছিলেন এবং এরপর একটি দিনের জন্যও তাদের একান্ত কাছে ডেকে এনে নিরিবিলি বসে হাতখানি হাতে ধরেননি কিংবা রূপসীর লাবণ্যময় মুখখানা দু-হাতে তুলে ধরে বলেননি, “আহারে সোনালি বন্ধু শুনিয়া যাও মোর কথা, হাছন রাজার হৃদয়কমলে তোমার চান্দমুখ গাঁথা ।” কিন্তু তাতে কি? কুমারী কন্যা তার জীবনের সেই ছয় কিংবা বারটি মাসের স্বর্ণময় সৃতি বুকে ধারণ করে বাকি জীবন কাটিয়ে দিয়েছেন।”

11. From the above quotation we find that there was nothing left for anyone else to damage the name, fame and saintliness of Hason Raja. The petitioner herself very efficiently did the job of tarnishing the image of her great grandfather and is now seen to be fiercely protecting the good name of Dewan Hasan Raja Chowdhury. This is a paradox. Having felled a beautiful tree full of fragrant flowers it is of no use and consequence now trying to blame others that they have cut down or pruned its branches in a cruel manner. The dead tree cannot be brought back to life through any mechanism, not even the intervention of the constitutional Court.

12. Mrs Sigma Huda raised the fundamental question of maintainability of the writ petition itself, contending, inter alia, that Hasan Raja died more than 80 years ago and a dead person cannot be defamed; that if anyone's religious feeling is hurt, he or she can take recourse to a suit for damages or for remedies available under the Censorship Act, inasmuch as Section 7 of the Censorship of Film Act, 1963 (Act XVIII of 1963) provides for de- certification of a film if the Government is of the opinion that a certified film or class of certified films should, in the interest of law and order, or in the interest of local film industry, or in any other national interest, be decertified in respect of the whole or any part of Bangladesh, it may of its own motion, by notification in the official gazette, direct that such film or class of films shall be deemed to be uncertified films in respect of the whole of Bangladesh or such area or areas as may be specified in the notification.

13. Furthermore, section 7(A) provides for seizure of the film while section 8 provides for penalty when the film does not show the mark of the authority or which has been altered or tampered within any way since such mark was affixed thereto, or contravenes any other provision of this Act or the Rules made thereunder, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to 10,000 Taka or with both. Sub-section (2) of section 8 provides that where a person is convicted of an offence punishable under sub-section (1) in respect of any film, the Court passing the sentence may further direct that the film shall be forfeited to the Government.

14. Mrs Huda emphatically argues that the alternative remedy not having been taken resort to, this writ petition is not maintainable. She further submits that the petitioner did not ask for any Rule to the effect that the certification of the film by the Film Censor Board be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect and that without making the substantial prayer there cannot be any prayer for consequential relief as has been made in this writ petition i.e. prayer for interlocutory relief in the shape of a restraining order i.e. to suspend the screening of the film till hearing of the Rule. Even if the Rule is made absolute, the Censorship Certificate would remain suspended only for so long as the Writ Petition is heard. But what would happen thereafter? Mrs Huda also argued that the petitioner misled the Court in describing Mr Helal Khan (respondent No. 3) As the director of the film. The Director is Mr Chashi Nazrul Islam.

15. Both the parties urged upon the Court to watch the film so that it can arrive at the proper decision as to whether the same contains any obscene, objectionable or outrageous material and as to whether Hason Raja has been depicted as someone or something which, in fact, he never was or, in other words, whether the person behind the persona was truly and faithfully revealed in the film.

16. While the film was projected in our presence as desired by both the parties, Mr Shorful Islam Khan pointed out that the scene showing Hason Raja embracing Binodini and the scene showing Hurmat Jahan Bibi, mother of Has on Raja, appearing at a Jalsha (জলসা) in the attire of a Professional dancer (বাইজি) are obscene and those 2 (two) sequences have hurt and outraged the religious sentiment of innumerable followers of the mystic poet and saint. To ascertain the correctness of the assertions of the learned Counsel for the petitioner, the alleged offending portions of the film were shown a second time but we could not find any material in support of his contention because those 2(two) sequences cannot evoke any anger or hateful reaction or response in the mind of a reasonable person or a common man in the street. Rather those 2(two) sequences lifted Hason Raja to a further and greater height. The scene showing Hason Raja and Binodini embracing each other did unfold the true saint that Hason was. It depicted how dispassionate he was and how quickly he reacted by ordering Binodini to leave his Zamindary at once when it dawned upon him that sensuality may engulf and overpower him if Benodini is around. And the Sequence at the Jalsha completely transformed the life of Has on Raja. His mother succeeded in making Hason shun the voluptuous propensity of a young and wealthy Zamindar which was the normal and usual way of life of a traditional Zamindar. When he crossed 60(sixty) Hason Raja kept no property for himself. He distributed all his properties including 3(three) hundred thousand bighas of land between his 2(two) sons and the other near and dear ones. Ultimately, Hason Raja completely withdrew himself from worldly life and his soul remained totally absorbed in the quest for the greater soul.

17. Hason Raja saw the light of this mundane world much later than Lalon Shah or Lalon Fakir. Hason Raja was born in 1885 and died in 1992 but no one knows the date or even the year when Lalon was born or died. Furthermore, no one is sure and certain as to whether Lalon was a Muslim or a Hindu. According to some disciples and followers, he was a Hindu while according to some he was a Muslim. When Hindus claim that Lalon was a Hindu the Muslims do not drag the matter to Court on the plea that the religious sentiment of the Muslims is hurt and so is the scenario when Muslims claim that Lalon was a Muslim. Does it matter whether he was a Hindu or a Muslim? Lalon is Lalon. Only he can be his equal and so is Hason Raja. He cannot be lowered down because he never stooped low. The perennial and persistent quest of his life was, Who am I? Where have I come from? And where shall I go? He composed meditative songs and sang those with the fullest devotion. He had no lust for wealth and sex. He found himself lost in the depth of spiritualism and that is why he was able to shun the glitter of gold. It may not be out of place to mention that once when his mother Hurmat Jahan entreated Hason to replace the mud- walled house with a building saying, “হাসান তুই স্রিহট্ট জেলার সবচেয়ে বড় জমিদার । তোর তিন লক্ষ বিঘা জমি। তুই কেন মাটির ঘরে থাকিস? লোকে মন্দ বলে।” instantaneously the young Zamindar took a musical instrument and sang a song, a portion of which is quoted below:

“লোকে বলে, বলেরে ঘর বাড়ী ভালা না আমার,

কি ঘর বানাইমু আমি শূন্যেরো মাঝার ।

এই ভাবিয়া হাছন রাজায় ঘর-দুয়ার না বান্দে,

কোথায় নিয়া রাখবো আল্লায় তার লাগিয়া কান্দে।

ভালা কইরা ঘর বানাইয়া থাকমু কত আর,

আয়না দিয়া চাইয়া দেখি পাক না চুল আমার।

আগে যদি জানতাম হাছন বাঁচব কতদিন,

বানাইত দালানকোঠা করিয়া রঙ্গীন।”

18. This song very amply conveys the message as to how strong a sense of detachment grew in Hason Raja who was at the time very rich, powerful, healthy, handsome, emotional, romantic and, above all, young.

19. The petitioner though is the descendant of Hason Raja, she cannot lay a claim that the saintly poet is her personal property or, for that matter, her family property or possession. Hason belongs to the nation and to the world at large. He cannot be diminished, compartmentalised and kept confined within the geographical boundary of Sylhet or, for that matter, Bangladesh. Kalidas, Balmiki, Shakespeare, Shelly, Keats, Byron, Rabindra Nath Tagore, Sir Iqbal and Kazi Nazrul Islam are the properties of the whole world and so are Lalon and Hason. The petitioner cannot have any monopoly, over Hason Raja more so because she herself having deliberately and consciously wounded and injured the image of Hason Raja has now appeared on the scene as a warrior to save and protect his image. This is a double standard and she is blowing hot and cold in the same breath.

20. There can be no dispute or debate that Hason Raja was not a Prophet like Jesus Christ (Isha Nabi) and Mohammad (Sm) and there can be no comparison of Hason Raja either with Isha Nabior Prophet Mohammad (Sm). But even then in the year 1988 there was an attempt to find out who was Jesus. The Time Magazine in an article on religion under the heading "A Holy Furor" reviewed the film. The story unfolds like this "Jesus has brief on- screen sex with his first wife Mary Magdalene and later commits adultery. Judas is a hero, the strongest and best of the apostles. Paul is a hypocrite and liar. Jesus is so dazed that, even on the eve of his crucifixion, he is still not quite sure whether to preach love or murder Romans".

21. Powerful, eccentric, bloody, filled with theological gaffes, "Temptation is an excruciatingly earnest and freewheeling docudrama based on 1955 best selling novel by a tormented Greek Orthodox believer; Nikos Kazantzakis. It is the result of an obsessive 16-year quest by one of Hollywood's most esteemed directors to bring to the screen a struggling Christ who only slowly comes to see himself as the Messiah. The movie, Scorsese says, "is my way of trying to get closer to God."

22. Italian Director Zeffirelli called the movie "damaging to the image of Christ. He cannot be made the object of low fantasies:" Fundamentalist Leader Jerry Falwell called for a boycott against MCA, Universal's parent company; all MCA products, which include Grosset & Dunlap publishers, Spencer Gifts and Motown Records; and any the atre that shows the film. Said Falwell: "Neither the label 'fiction' nor the First Amendment gives Universal the height to libel, slander and ridicule the most central figure in world history."

23. To head off further furor or perhaps even cash in on it, Universal decided last week to move the opening up from September 23 to August 12. Says Tom Pollock, Chairman of MCA's motion picture group: "The best thing that can be done for "The Last Temptation of Christ" at this time is to make it available to the American people and allow them to draw their own conclusions, based on fact not fallacy." But Tim Penland, a born-again marketing expert once hired by Universal to placate conservative critics and now a critic himself, believes the six-week jump will unleash more Fundamentalist anger. ''It's the most serious mistake a studio has. made in decades," he says.

24. The dramatic centerpiece of the film is a half-hour segment in which the dying Christ, played by Willem Dafoe, hallucinates about the devil's final temptation: come down from the Cross, renounce your role as the Messiah, marry Mary Magdalene and live a long and ordinary life.

25. Nothing unorthodox there, strictly speaking. As both fully human and fully divine, Jesus is viewed in Christian theology as free of sin but subject to all temptations, including sexual ones. Following Kazantzakis, however, Scorsese presents the early Jesus as a weak and dithering collaborator who builds crosses used by the Romans to execute Jewish rebels. Later he becomes the wild-eyed guru to a band of ragged followers but remains apprehensive and fundamentally confused about his message and his mission. He persuades Judas, his best friend, to betray him to fulfil God's plan. During the reverie on the Cross, Jesus is shown briefly having sex with his wife, Mary Magdalene Later in the fantasy, after Magdalene dies, he weds Mary of the biblical duo Mary and Martha, then commits adultery with Martha.

26. "Temptation" is drenched in blood. The blood of sacrificed animals runs through the streets, blood unaccountably pours out of an apple Jesus eats and, at the Last Supper, the wine literally turns into blood. In one grotesque scene, Jesus reaches into his chest (though it looks more like his belly), yanks out his heart and holds it up for his apostles to admire.

27. For a few critics, this display seems to be an arch send-up of the Catholic devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus. Some dialogue also hints at satire, probably unintentionally. Asked by a Zealot to compare being dead with being alive, the resurrected Lazarus says thought fully was a little surprised. There isn't that much difference." At times Jesus sounds like a mumbling method actor (his first sermon begins "Umm, uh, I'm sorry"), at others like a recent graduate of the Shirley MacLaine school of Theology ("Everything's part of God").

28. For Scorsese, a former altar boy who once wanted to be a priest, the movie is no frivolous matter. Actress Barbara Hershey, who plays Mary Magdalene, gave him a copy of the Kazantzakis novel in 1972, and he has been contemplating it ever since. Kazantzakis' Jesus, he insists, is both human and divine, in accordance with Christian teaching. What interested Scorsese in the author's approach "was that the human part of Jesus would have trouble accepting the divine."

29. For many believers, the problem with all this is that Scorsese is not tinkering with a minor historical figure, as Gore Vidal did with Aaron Burr, but with the founder of their faith. "This is an intentional attack on Christianity," concludes Joseph Reilly, national director of Morality in Media. The group is particularly incensed by Jesus' anguished comment, "I am a liar, and I am a hypocrite. I am afraid of everything.... Lucifer is inside me."

30. Universal Pictures had anticipated controversy. Paramount, originally set to produce the movie in 1983, backed out just weeks before the cameras were to roll. To head off a storm, Universal took the unusual step last January of hiring Penland to calm down the religious right. But Penland resigned in June, charging that Universal had reneged on a promise to let conservative religious leaders see the film and comment on it well in advance of its release.

31. Although Universal did hold screenings for religious leaders last month, most conservatives refused to come. Instead they staged protests at the Universal lot and published an admonishing ad in the Hollywood Reporter. In a letter to MCA Chairman Lew Wasserman, Bill Bright of the Campus Crusade for Christ offered to raise money to reimburse Universal for all copies of the film, which would "promptly be destroyed". Universal responded with lofty, full-page newspaper ads in four cities, quoting Thomas Jefferson and announcing that the constitutional rights to free expression and freedom of religion were not for sale.

32. In the most organised campaign of resistance, Methodist Minister Donald Wildmon, head of the American Family Association, is sending out 2.5 million mailings protesting the film and has scheduled anti-Temptation spots on 700 Christian radio stations and 50 to 75 TV stations. "In the twelve years of my current ministry," he says, "I have never seen anything like the response to this movie."

33. Make that the response to the response. As an annoyed Scorsese points out, "Ninety-nine percent of the people who are complaining have not seen the picture." Many complainers are instead responding to a bootleg copy of an outdated script, circulated by the Sisterhood of Mary, a group of ultraconservative Protestant women. That version contained the egregious line, which is not in the movie, spoken by Jesus to Mary Magdalene: "God sleeps between your legs."

34. Universal has tried to calm things down, inserting a disclaimer in the movie saying it is fiction and making Scorsese available for interviews stressing his religious sincerity. Yet the protest has taken on a life of its own. Virtually every televangelist, including Pat Robertson, has mentioned the film during appeals for money. A nonsectarian group called Concerned Women for America has asked all MCA stockholders to sell the company's stock on September 15. And Mother Angelica, a nun who runs the nation's largest Catholic cable network, is calling on protesters to drive with their lights on August 22. Both dates were picked at random when the opening was still set for September.

35. Some of the protests have taken on ugly anti-Semitic overtones. Three weeks ago, the Rev RL Hymers Jr., a Christian extremist in the Los Angeles area, staged a demonstration near the Beverly Hills home of MCA Chairman Wasserman, who is Jewish. An actor portraying Wasserman stepped repeatedly on the bloody back of an actor dressed as Jesus and carrying a heavy cross. An airplane meanwhile flew overhead trailing a banner that read, Wasserman Fans Jew-Hatred W/Temptation and a crowd chanted, "Bank rolled by Jewish money."

36. As conservatives shriek all around them, liberal churchmen have been bending over backward to avoid criticising the film, stressing Scorsese's right to interpret Jesus in his own way and sometimes issuing a tepid defence or two. Fundamentalist fears are exaggerated, says the Rev Eugene Schneider of the United Church of Christ, because "people who go to the movie are going to come out bored and leave before it is over."

37. The Rt Rev Paul Moore Jr., Episcopal Bishop of New York, offered one of the strongest defences, calling "Temptation" "theologically sound." Though the love-making between Jesus and Mary Magdalene may offend some, he said, "Remember, it's a dream. This is yet another portrait-a work of· art which emphasises certain aspect, of Jesus." The Rev William Fore of the National Council of Churches similarly sees the movie as "an honest attempt to tell the story of Jesus from a different perspective".

38. Catholics and Methodists have issued no formal response to the film. Bishop Anthony Bosco of Greensburg, Pa, head of the communications department for the National Council of Catholic Bishops thinks that the movie should be allowed to expire quietly. "This too shall pass away," he says. But not all Catholics are so patient: his office has received hundreds of phone calls demanding that the church speak out. Says Bishop Bosco: "The anti-Semitism and the hatred this movie has caused can hardly please the heart of Christ."

39. Many clergymen say they have no interest in fanning hysteria over the film, but they wish that Scorsese had made a better movie. The film's Jesus questions himself so much that "it's sort of like watching The Three Faces of Eve," complains the Rev Michael Morris, who teaches religion and the cinema at a Catholic school in Berkeley.

40. There are knotty theological problems too. In the dream sequence, for example, when Jesus interrupts Paul's preaching to explain that he did not die and rise again, Paul says the facts are not important as long as people have something to believe in. This appears to reinforce the familiar and cynical view that Paul invented Christianity and distorted Jesus' teachings. Scorsese's Jesus also makes a number of doctrinal blunders. He announces that his death will pay for his own sins, rather than for the sins of mankind. And he picks up dirt and stones and says, "This is my body too," which apparently makes him a founder of pantheism as well as Christianity.

41. Such theological slipups are fueling passions about the film. Father Morris says he was told by Scorsese that the filmmaker wonders why everyone is so upset when "it's just a movie." After the entire director said he has a right to work out his private quest for Jesus on film. "This irks me a bit," admits Father Morris. You can't be working out private problems to the degree that it causes people to riot in the streets. Although that prospect is unlikely, "The Last Temptation" has touched off the angriest religious debate in years."

42. Against the screening of the film "The Last Temptation of Christ" there was no Writ Petition before the High Court Division though Jesus Christ is our Prophet too. A few weeks back an English clergyman had the bad taste of saying that Mary was not a virgin mother. She was raped by a Roman soldier, got pregnant and gave birth to Jesus Christ. And this time also no Writ petition was filed by anyone before this Court or in any other Court. People like Lalon Fakir and Hason Raja not being Prophets, how can Article 102 of the Constitution be invoked to stop or prevent the film maker i.e. Chashi Nazrul Islam from making the film the way it was made, with a prayer to suspend the certificate issued by the Chairman, Film Censor Board (respondent No. 1) till the hearing of the Rule?

<u>43. We had the added advantage of watching the film which started with a young man on horse- back galloping through a bamboo clump and on the way having seen some rustic damsels bathing in a pond commented “এই মুনিয়া পাখিরা, কেমন আছ তোমরা? অদ্য চলিলাম বন্ধু, কল্য দেখা হইবে।” The rider went on and on the way having come across a poor young but pretty girl carrying a pitcher on her waist, halted the horse, came back and stood in front of the bewildered girl and threw away his gold necklace towards the girl and galloped away without a word. The man on horse-back was none else than Hason Raja, a Zaminder's son having three lac bighas of land. He was young, very handsome, hot-blooded and romantic with all the power and wealth at his disposal and having found a helpless rustic girl all alone in a bamboo clump did neither kiss nor touch the girl though he could have had all the liberties he wished for because the girl was completely infatuated and was ready and willing to surrender to the young man with an honest belief that she was married to Hason Raja (Her God). The sequences taken exception and objected to by Mr Shorful Islam Khan, in our opinion, did in no way adversely affect the saintly image of Hason Raja. On the contrary, he was lifted up far above the height of the ordinary mortals like us. The scene showing Hason Raja embracing Binodidi is a manifestation of self- restraint, strong discipline of mind and quick realisation and consequent return to the right path by a young man having enormous wealth of all kinds. The moment he realised that his infatuation for Binodini is not approved by good sense and morality Hason Raja made a sharp 'U turn' which very few people of his age and advantage could have done. This scene has, we think, glorified Hason Raja instead of villifying and castigating him which, according to Mr Khan, had hurt the religious sentiment and feeling of the disciples and admirers of Hason Raja.</u>

44. The film depicted Hason Raja as an efficient, strict, and cruel at times but at most of the time he was shown to be a very kind-hearted and generous Zamindar doling out favours to his poor subjects including Binodini. Binodini undertook a long and hard journey to Luxmonsree from Rampasha accompanied by her guardian grandfather carrying with her the necklace given by Hason Raja without dismounting from the horse he was riding. On her grandfather's query as to why they were going to Luxmonsree, the reply from Binodini was“আমি আমার দেবতাকে দেখতে যাব।”It was an one-sided love affair by Binodini even whenthe Zamindar allowed Binodini and her grandfather to settle at Luxmonsree by allotting some land without rent (লাখেরাজ) It was at a later stage that the young Zamindar was attracted to much more younger Binodini who possessed beauty both in its raw and sublime manifestation. Binodini as she believed rightly or wrongly that she was married to Hason Raja naturally developed a sense of possession and laid a claim upon Hason Raja and on being asked by Hason, immediately after he got himself released from the embracing arms of Binodini as to what she expects from him saying, " তুমি কি চাও?" The prompt reply from Binodini was "তোমাকে চাই" And the equally prompt and sharp reply of Hason was, "তোমরা সবাই আমাকে চাও, আমি কি করবো? আমার স্ত্রী আছে, পুত্র আছে। হে মাবুদ দুনিয়াতে এত পাপ কেন?"

45. And immediately thereafter with a very heavy heart he asked Binodini to leave his Zamindary which she did. This drastic but painful decision had a devastating effect on Hason Raja's vivacious life style. He ceased to compose and sing and told his mother Hurmat Jahan Bibi, who gave a handsome amount of money to Binodini and asked her to quit Luxmonsree for Brindaban or Kashi (Benaras), as to the cause of his depressions "মা আমার গানের পাখী উড়ে গেছে, আর গান গাইতে পারি না।"But he made no attempt to bring back Binodini which he could have easily done thus making it clear that he had no lust for the flesh of Binodini. Binodini was just a source of inspiration to Hason Raja for his faculty to compose songs which were no ordinary songs. Hason's love for Binodini was more metaphysical than physical or, in other words, it was an episode of platonic love. Hason Raja had although been longing for getting united with the greater soul i.e. the Creator, in the fashion and manner as that of Mansur Hallaj who succeeded in attaining the stage called "Fanafilla" (ফানাফিল্লা) 1 We know that Mansur Hallaj was misunderstood by the Muslim clerics who prevailed upon the state machinery and got Mansur Hallaj declared a heretic and had him killed.

46. All human beings have in them a small fraction of the greater soul which eagerly awaitsreunion with the greater soul. The reality of the longing of small soul in us with the greater soul i.e. the Creator, is manifested in the saying "Flame goes up, why? Because it yearns for its greater form which is the sun. A clod of mud falls down. Why? To join its greater form, the Earth. The air in a balloon escapes if it can. Why? To join its greater form, the outer air. So also the soul in our bodies longs to join the greater world soul." And the soul of Hason Raja had a fierce longing and yearning because it was not as ordinary as ours.

47. In the film, we found Hason Raja very depressed after the departure of Binodini and to overcome the same a "Jalsha" was arranged and a Baizee from Lucknow was hired. But through the contrivance of Hurmat Jahan and the Naib of the Estate, Hurmat, mother of the young Zamindar, in a desperate attempt to bring back her son to the line of her forefathers appeared at the Jalsha in the disguise of a "Baizee". Little did Hason know that the Baizee was none else than his revered mother. Hason received her with utmost courtesy and politeness unlike the fellow Rajas in the assembly. And the moment Hurmat Jahan lifted her veil, Hason fell on the feet of his mother and begged for mercy. The mother was ice-cold in her response. She did not forgive her son and left the scene expressing her last wish in the following words "আমার অস্তিমকালে আমার সন্তান যেন আমার মুখ দেখতে না পায়।" Immediately thereafter she fell ill and eventually died without ever seeing the face of her only son Hason Raja. The passing away of his mother had a profound effect on the mystic and romantic poet, singer and the young but very powerful Zamindar. There occurred a complete transformation. Hason Raja gave up worldly life and became a Sufi Saint completely detached from the life he had hitherto been living.

<u>48. Nowhere in the film was there any sexuality nor was there any sensual import of any kind. It is not understood how the 'Jalsha' scene could be described as obscene, immoral, indecent and ugly. In present day Bangladesh films are made mostly to cater to and suit the taste of the uneducated working class, particularly the rickshaw pullers and day labourers. Those filmscannot be watched by family comprising parents, sons and daughters. Besides these, many of the films are infested not only with obscenity but with violence. In that respect the film 'Hason Raja' stands on a very exalted and high platform, free from sex and violence which is the standard of the day. The film in question appears to us to be a clean one. When a Prophet such as Isha Nabi (Jesus Christ) is labelled as an adulterer, liar and, above all, an illegitimate child of Mary who was allegedly impregnated by a Roman soldier, religious sentiment of the people of this country, particularly the petitioner, was not hurt or outraged. So, why a film depicting the life of a saint containing 2(two) sequences i.e. the embracing of Binodini by young Hason which was not one/sided and the appearance of Hunnat Jahan at the Jalsha in the guise of a Baizee, should be condemned by canceling the certificate issued by the Film Censor Board? We find nothing wrong in granting the certificate by the Film Censor Board.</u>

49. Mrs Sigma Huda, learned Counsel for respondent No. 3, urged upon the Court to award cost for causing huge financial loss and inconvenience to her client for sheer greed of the petitioner Sadia Chowdhury Porag by obtaining an order of stay of the release of the film. She claims Taka 1 (one) million per day which by any standard is a fabulous amount and Mr Sharful Islam Khan, learned Counsel for the petitioner, submits that if cost is awarded, the petitioner would be confronted with a serious predicament because being poor and indigent she would not be in a position to pay cost and urged upon the Court to be generous in not awarding any cost and that his client honestly believed that the image of her illustrious ancestor was lowered down by the film. Mrs Huda however submits that the petitioner having herself sufficiently damaged and lowered her great grandfather cannot be allowed to say that she made an honest attempt to protect the image of Hason Raja.

50. Regard being had to the facts and circumstances of the case, the submissions of the learned Counsel of both sides and for the fore going reasons, we are of the opinion that ends of justice would be met if the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost, however, with a note of warning and caution to petitioner Sadia Chowdhury Porag not to indulge in such activities in future.

In the result the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost. The Producer and Director of the film "Hason Raja" are at liberty to release/screen the film without any hindrance from anyone.

End.

lawyer:
Moudud Ahmed with Azizul Hoque Advocates ----- For the Petitioner [In WP No. 1787 of 1998] 
Obaidur Rahman Mostafa, Deputy Attorney General with Dr Quazi Rezaul Hoque, Assistant Attorney General ----- For tire Respondents

full_judgment:
Md Muzammel Hossain J: Rules in Writ Petition No. 1787 of 1998 and Writ Petition No. 2259 of 1998 have been heard analogously and are being disposed of this single judgment since common question, of law and facts are involved in both the

2. In Writ Petition No. 1787of 1998 Rule was issued at the instance of the petitioner, Abdul Mannan, calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 9-6-98 issued by the respondent No. 2 and Final Notification as to the Delimitation of nine wards of Lalmohan Pourashava should not be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

3. In Writ Petition No. 1787 of 1998 the petitioners case, in brief, for disposal of the Rule is as follows: The petitioner is a Commissioner of newly created ward No. 4 (Old) Ward No. 2) of Lalmohan Pourashava in the District of Bhola. The petition is directed against the impugned and order namely, Churanta Biggaptti (Final Notification) issued by the respondent No. 2, Thana Nirbahi Officer and Delimitation Officer, vide Memo No. Thana/NI/AD-Lal-98-745 (500) dated 9-6-98 (Annexure-A) in respect of delimitation of three wards into nine wards of Lalmohan Pourashava. The delimitation awards were made under section 21 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 by the said notification. The authority Preserves (one) seat for women to be elected from 3(three) wards as a result there are 3 female candidates who would be elected from the newly created nine wards. In issuing the Final Notification the respondents did not follow the provisions of section 21 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977. According to section 21(1) of Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 the wards shall be delimited having regard to territorial unit, distribution of population save with a valuation of not more than 10% administrative convenience. But the respondent No. 2 made a final notification without considering the territorial units, distribution of population and administrative convenience. He also did not make some inquiries and examination of records and consideration of the opinions of the people before publishing the notice in violation of sub-section 2 of section 21 of the said Ordinance. The respondent No. 4 Deputy Secretary (Poura) by his letter dated the 2nd March, 1998 on top priority basis informed the respondent No. 2, Delimitation Officer, and others including the Chairman Lalmohan Pourashava stating that the government was going to delimitate three wards of the Lalmohan Pourashava into nine wards having regard to section 21(1) to the effect that area and voter wise delimitation of respective wards shall not be varied by more' than 10%. After suppressing the said letter dated the 23rd March, 1998 the respondents No. 2 had issued a letter to the Chairman, Lalmohan Pourashava , under his memo No. 98/401 dated 19-4-98 stating that Lalmphan Pourashava is going to be delimitated from three wards to nine wards as desired by the government and asked him to give specific thoughtful proposal within three days as to how the wards would be newly created. On 21st April, 1998 the Lalmohan Pourashava has sent specific proposal under Memo No. Laupoura/Admn/98-104 (Annexure-D) stating in details of the areas with the boundary of the nine wards along with the map. Without providing any opportunity of hearing to the Pourashava Chairman and the Commissioner, the respondent No. 2 published the newly created nine wards and invited objections and suggestions from the public against the said newly created nine wards. Lalmohan Pourashava made strong representation on 31-5-98 to respondent No. 2 stating that the said nine newly created wards disestablished the socio-structural boundary with population. Without hearing the Pourashava Commissioners and the Chairman the respondent No. 2 sent his proposed delimitation of wards report to the Ministry. Then the respondent No. 4 vide his memo No. Poura-2/Ward-6/98/796 dated 4-6-98 (Annexure-E) advised the Delimitation Office and the Deputy Commissioner, Bhola that 7-6-98 was fixed for hearing of the objection preliminary list in the Secretariat and asked the concerned parties to remain present to discuss about pros and cons as to delimitation of wards relating to objections, suggestions and proposals. On 5-6-98 the respondent No. 2 informed the petitioner to remain present and raise the objections suggestion about the said delimitation. In the Secretariat the respondent No. 4 did not give the petitioners and others any opportunity of hearing on the delimitation of said wards rather he arranged mockery of the hearing. According to the latest voter lists if it is compared with the present alleged final notification as to the delimitation of nine wards in respect of voter numbers, namely, Ward No. 4 which is having 1023 voters, Ward No. 6 is having 1235 voters. Ward No. 8 is having 1235 voters whereas the other wards namely, Ward No. 1 is having 562 voters, Ward No. 2- is having 822 voters, Ward No. 3 is having 684 voters, Ward No. 5 is having 873 voters, Ward No. 7 is having 647 voters and Ward No. 9 is having 742 voters, copy of the said figures of voters in the newly created nine wards supplied by the Chairman of the Lalmohan Pourashava has been marked as Annexure-F. The respondent No. 4, Deputy Secretary vide his letter dated 22-3-98 asked the respondent No. 2 to delimit the Lalmohan Pourashava into 9 wards in place of 3 wards according to section 21 of the Ordinance of 1977 within one month but before the expiry of the period of one month on 19-4-98 he simply gave a notice to Lalmohan Pourashava with 3 days’ notice asking them to supply him with facts and figures of voters area wise with up to date Pourashava map and boundary. The petitioners gave their proposed report with map etc. to the respondent No. 2 over the said proposed boundary of the wards along with the population of the Pourashava which has not been taken into consideration by the respondent No. 2. The respondent No. 2 without making any publicity and without hearing the Commissioners and Chairman of the Lalmohan Pourashava at the instance of the interested quarters sent his delimitation reports to the Ministry for its approval. The Ministry did not give the petitioners any opportunity to place their things in proper way. The respondent No. 1 hurriedly made their arrangement at their own accord and subsequent final notification (impugned order Annexure-A) has been publish6d in violation of section 21 of the Ordinance without looking into distribution of population, territorial unity and administrative convenience, representation of the Pourashava Committee. Thus the final notification to the delimitation of the wards of Lalmohan Pourashava has not been done in accordance with law and is of no legal effect.

4. The petitioner so filed in the course of hearing a supplementary affidavit annexing a memorandum issued to the Chairman, Lalmohan Pourashava by the Thana Statistical Officer, Lalmohan, Bhola under memo No. 30/99 dated 17-2-99 (Annexure-II) giving in details ward wise population of the said nine wards. It is stated that most of the wards varies more than 10% population.

5. The respondent Nos. 1 and 2 contested the Rule on the same grounds by filing two separate affidavits-in-opposition denying statements made in the writ petition stating, inter cilia, that the respondent No. 2, Delimitation Officer as per provisions of section 21 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 delimited the wards of Lalmohan Pourashava having regard to the territorial unity and so far as practicable to distribution of population and administrative convenience. The Delimitation Officer, respondent No. 2 by Memo dated 19-4-1998 invited proposal from the people of the Pourashava and he received proposals and comments from several persons, and Lalmohan Pourashava Parishad. Thereafter, the Delimitation Officer visited the entire Pourashava area, prepared trace map, with plot number of different mouzas and delimited the existing 3 wards into 9 Wards and 3 reserved seats for women and then as per section 21(2) he published the preliminary list of proposed nine wards with a notice on 17-5-1998 inviting objections and suggestions within 15 days from the date of publication of the notice. Accordingly, twelve objections were filed and received. As per section 21(3) of the Ordinance, 1977 all objections and suggestions were sent by the Delimitation Officer to the prescribed authority who on receipt of those fixed 7-6-1998 for hearing and enquiry and accordingly, notices were issued to Thana. Nirbahi Officer (Delimitation Officer) and other concerned persons. After conclusion of hearing on 7-6-98 before the prescribed authority a decision was given requiring some amendments and alterations of the preliminary list and the Delimitation Officer was directed by the prescribed authority to make necessary amendments on or before 10-6-98 and as per order of the prescribed authority, the Thana Nirbahi Officer, being the Delimitation Officer made necessary amendments and published the final list of delimited nine wards specifying the areas on 9-6-1998 and forwarded the sane to the Ministry for publication in the Official Gazette. The statements made in paragraph No. 1 of supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner is denied by the respondents. There was no ward wise population list lying with the government in accordance with the newly delimited 9 wards of Lalmohan Pourashava, rather the government is having record of the population of the earlier 3 Wards of Lalmohan Pourashava as per census held in 1991 through but the country and the Lalmohan Pourashava was established in 1990 and the population Of the earlier 3 wards is the basis of the present delimitation. Each earlier ward being converted into 3 wards by way of delimitation having regard to the territorial unity and so far as practicable to distribution of population and administrative convenience, The memorandum dated 17-2-99 issued by the Thana Statistical Officer to the Chairman, Lalmohan Pourashava (Annexure-II) is a false and fabricated document enacted for the purpose of this writ petition. The said memorandum (Annexure-II) has never been sent by the Thana Statistical Officer under his signature and, as such, the information contained in the memo is not correct and officially authenticated. The petitioner did not file any objection upon the said preliminary list and after completion of the final list of wards and publication of the same in official gazette on 2-7-1998 the writ petitioner on 9-7-98 challenged the final notification in the writ petition and obtained a Rule which is liable to be discharged. The respondent No. 2 completed the delimitation of 3 wards into 9 wards of Lalmohan Pourashava as per section 21 of the Ordinance, 1977 which is reflected in the official tile of delimitation wards of Lalmohan Pourashava being file No. 2-6/98 and the respondent No. 2 craves the leave of the court to produce the file at the time of hearing of the Rule.

6. The petitioner filed two separate affidavits-in-reply against the affidavits-in-opposition submitted by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 denying the statements made in the affidavits-in-opposition by the said respondents. The petitioner asserts that the memorandum dated 17-2-99 (Annexure-H) was issued by the Thana Statistical Officer which is a valid documents and in support of his contention he annexed a memo No. 91 dated 7-6-98 issued by the Thana Statistical Officer as Annexure-X showing the population distribution of the newly created 9 wards of Lalmohan Pourashava.

7. The respondent No. 2 filed supplementary affidavit denying the petitioners statement in the affidavit-in-reply and asserting that the memorandum Annexure-H alleged to have been issued by the Thana Statistical Officer is absolutely false and baseless and that no such statistics have been available in the said office on 7-2-99 which is evident from the memo No. 91 dated 7-6-99 Annexure-1) issued by the Thana Statistical Officer Lalmohan.

8. In Writ Petition No. 2259 of 1998 Rule was issued at the instance of the petitioners Mia Lutfi Hossain Khasru and 5 others calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why impugned notification dated 2nd July, 1998 (Annexure-L) as to delimitation of 9 wards of Choumuhani Pourashava Begumganj, District-Noakhali should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

9. In Writ Petition No. 2259 of 1998 the petitioner's case for disposal of the Rule is as follows: The petitioner No. 6 is the sitting elected Pourashava Chairman and the petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 are also sitting elected Commissioners of the said Pourashava. Petitioner No. 4 is also a former Union Parishad Member. The respondent No. 1, is the 'Secretary and the respondent Nos. 2, 3 and 4 are the concerned government officers those who are directly or indirectly connected with the affairs of the present impugned notification published on 2nd July, 1998 after the delimitation of 3 wards into 9 wards of Choumuhani Pourashava. The respondent No. 2 under Memo No Poura-2/Ward-6/98/375 (526) dated 22-3-98 (Annexure-A) informed the Deputy Commissioner, Additional Deputy Commissioner and others by appointing Thana Nirbahi Officer, Begumganj, as Delimitation Officer and Assistant Commissioner (Land) as Assistant Delimitation Officer in accordance with section 20 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 for delimitation of 9 wards from the existing 3 wards of Choumuhani Pourashava. In the said memo the delimitation officers was specifically, advised to take into consideration that population should be varying more or less 10% from one ward to another ward. The Delimitation Officer was directed to complete delimitation of the wards within one month on receipt the said memo and to report to the Ministry. The Chairman of the Pourashava was not informed about it after lapse of more than a month on 6-5-98. The respondent No. 4 after making delimitation of 9 wards from 3 wards served notices upon various persons including the Chairman, Choumuhani Pourashava who received the same on 14-4-98. The chairman of the Pourashava informed him specifically stating that the report has been made on 6-5-98 but served upon him on 14-5-98 and requested the respondent No. 4 to supply the details of the delimitation of the aforesaid wards but he never gave reply of the request made by the Pourashava Chairman of Choumuhani nor given any opportunity to be heard. It is stated that Md Ali Haider, former Member of the Union Parishad and 12 other persons of the Pourashava made a representation to respondent No. 4 giving details as to how 3 wards would be delimited 3 wards into 9 ward's and had shown details in its proper perspective for the betterment of the Pourashava delimitation keeping in mind of the number of Pourashava voters, etc. The respondent No. 4 in violation of section 21 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 has made out a report by delimiting 3 wards into 9 wards of the said Pourashava and sent the report to the Ministry of Local Government and Co-operative. Respondent No. 4 most arbitrarily at the instance of some interested quarters made delimitation from 3 wards into 9 wards without consideration of the territorial unity as far as practicable to distribution of population with a variation of not more than 10% and administrative convenience. In violation of section 21(2) of the said Ordinance the respondent No. 4 did not give any opportunity of hearing of the local people on their objections. Though the petitioner and others filed objections and suggestions the respondent's No. 4 did not even forward the same to the government nor he had sent the voter lists and the number of population in the respective wards along with the report. The petitioner on receipt of the information of delimitation, while the respondent No. 4 had sent report of the same to the concerned Ministry, submitted a representation to the Ministry on 27-5-98 stating in details of the area/mouza in respect of wards with voter numbers. etc as far as possible. The respondent No. 2 vide memo No. Poura-2LWard-6/98/71(5) dated 27-5-98 informed the petitioner No. 1 to remain present on 31st May 1998 for hearing which 'would take place before Md Maksumul Huq, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Local Government, according to section 21(2) and (3) of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977. On 6-6-98 respondent No. 4 under memo No. 433 after making some sort of amendment and changes worse than the earlier delimitation one sent it according to his sweet will to the Ministry giving a copy to the Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali and without giving a copy to the petitioner and Chairman of the Pourashava and others. The respondent No. 4 Thana Nirbahi Officer on 6-6-98 had shown the voter figure 3200 in Ward No. 4 and the line of delimitation of this ward also had taken shape in violation of the terms and conditions, namely, the unity of the wards as per section 21(1) on that score in the Ward Nos. 8 and 9. According to his report, voters were 2750 and 2700 receptively and the would not have been 10% variation of the 3 wards had the natural boundary, either the rail line or the canal (Choumuhani Atiahari Khal), been taken into consideration but after crossing the rail line as well as the said canal it came to the extent of some portion of Nos. 8 and 9 wards which is outright violation of territorial unity as well as variation of 10% voter. The report which he supplied for publication in the gazette notification as to the delimitation of 9 wards with its voters list with population is at variation with the report of the voters list he supplied to the Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali. The respondent No. 4 did not give any opportunity of hearing to the petitioners in spite of their representations before him nor he applied his mind towards the objections and representations as submitted by the petitioner and others. The delimitation of 3 wards of Choumuhani Pourashava into 9 wards have been made without lawful authority.

10. In Writ Petition No. 2259 of 1998 the respondents contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition denying the statements made in the writ petition and stating that the writ petition is not maintainable since it raises disputed question of fact. The writ petition has been filed with malafide intention to hold up the Pourashava election and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. The proposed delimitation notice was published on 6-6-95 in very specific and conspicuous terms in Bangla which were quite understandable by every resident of the Pourashava. The petitioner No. 6, the Chairman of the Choumuhani Pourashava, assisted in the said process of delimitation in question and a map regarding the same was also supplied by the Pourashava Chairman's Office. During the process of delimitation of Choumuhani Pourashava territorial unity, practicable distribution of population as required by the provision of law and administrative convenience were taken into consideration. The respondent No. 4, the Delimitation Officer, as per provision of section 21 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 delimited 3 wards into 9 wards of the Choumuhani Pourashava after examining all records, considering the-representations received by him published the preliminary list of wards specifying the areas with notice inviting objections and suggestions, fixing it in conspicuous places for mass attention and circulation. Objections and suggestions were forwarded to the Ministry by the respondent No. 4 and the petitioners and other objectors were given opportunity of hearing before the prescribed authority in the Ministry when the respondent No. 4 was present. Then the prescribed authority gave its decision for amendments and alterations and accordingly, the respondent No. 4 made necessary amendments and alterations in the preliminary list of wards and sent the final list to the prescribed authority in the Ministry for notification in the official Gazette. It is stated that as territorial boundary previous ward demarcation was given preference and indivisibility of market area of Choumuhani Bazar was also taken into consideration with an end of future administrative purpose. Golabaria area was previously included within Bazar and at present also that is kept in the same ward. For the purpose of protecting the indivisibility of the market canal was considered as a natural demarcation and, as such, a portion of Alipur mouza was kept with ward No. 4 which is better from the administrative point of view. It is not a fact that in respect of ward Nos. 1, 2 or 3 respondent No. 4 did not take into consideration the natural boundary namely, Sonaimuri-Maijdee C&B Road, or Choumuhani-Laximpur C&B road or that as a result 104 variation occurred in respect of voters in these three wards. In making delimitation of wards contiguous Union Parishad boundary and roads under R&H. Department and internal canal and important roads of the Pourashava and mouza boundary were taken into consideration. The petitioner No. 1 is a Commissioner, petitioner No. 4 is a contractor and the petitioner No. 6 is the Chairman of the Choumuhani Pourashava and they being members of the same family hail from the village Nazirpur and they had served several meetings with the respondent No. 4 and they are concerned at the behest of their ill motivated interests to dominate the will of the people through self-dictated delimitation and to delay the Pourashava election.

11. The petitioners filed an affidavit-in-reply against the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondents denying the allegations/statements made in the affidavit-in-opposition and reiterating the statements made in the writ petition and annexing two documents namely, an application dated 10-5-99 written by the Chairman of Choumuhani Pourashava requesting the Thana Statistical Officer to supply ward wise number of Population (Annexure-O) and in reply the Thana Statistical Officer, Begumganj on 10-5-99 informed the fact that after 1991 no census has taken place till today and he has given by memo dated 10-5-99 (Annexure-0-1) village-wise population of the former 3 wards of Choumuhani Pourashava. They also asserted that there was variations of population in the delimited 9 wards.

12. The petitioner also filed a supplementary affidavit annexing memo Nos. 424 and 423 issued by the Secretary Choumuhani Pourashava stating that population of village and ward wise of nine wards of Pourashava which showed variation of the population is more than 10% in the respective ward and the other letter giving the figure of population of each and every ward of nine wards of Choumuhani Pourashava.

13. In Writ Petition No. 1787 of 1998 Mr Moudud Ahmed, learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that delimitation of three wards into nine wards of Lalmohan Pourashava has been done without lawful authority and in violation of the provision of section 21 of Pourashava Ordinance, 1977. He then submits that sub-section 1 of section 21 of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 provides that wards shall be delimited having regard to territorial unity and so far as practicable to distribution of population save with a variation of not more than 10% and administrative convenience. He then refers to Annexures-A & H and submits that there has been clear violation of the mandatory provision of section 21(1) of the Ordinance, 1977 because of the variation of more than 10% as regards distribution of voters and population in the delimited 9 wards in the final list of wards published by the impugned order. The petitioner's contention relying on the alleged distribution of population stated in Annexure-H and X that most of the newly created wards varies more than 10% population having been denied by the respondents in their affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit and asserted that these are false and fabricated documents manufactured by the petitioner for the purpose of this writ petition which is evident from memo No. 91 dated 7-6-1999 (Annexure-1 to the supplementary affidavit) issued by the Thana Statistical Officer to the Thana Nirbahi Officer, respondent No. 2 stating to the following effect:

“উপরোক্ত বিষয়ে ও সূত্রের আলোকে জানানো যাচ্ছে যে, লালমোহন পৌর সভার নবগঠিত ৯টি ওয়ার্ডের জনসংখ্যার যে তথ্য চাওয়া হয়েছে তা অত্রাফিসে থেকে সরবরাহ করার কোন সুযোগ নাই। যেহেতু পৌরসভার ৯টি ওয়ার্ড সৃষ্টির অর্থাৎ ১৯৯১ সনের গত বাংলাদেশ পরিসংখ্যান ব্যুরো কর্তৃক কোন শুমারী জরিপ অনুষ্ঠিত হয়নি। ইতিপূর্বে প্রাক্তন থানা পরিসংখ্যান কর্মকর্তা কিভাবে লালমোহন পৌরসভাকে ৯টি নবগঠিত ওয়ার্ডের জন সংখ্যার তথ্য পরিবেশন করেছেন তারও কোন রেকর্ড পত্র অত্রাফিসে সংরক্ষিত নেই। এ ছাড়া পূর্ণাঙ্গ শুমারী ব্যতীত জনসংখ্যার তথ্য আদৌ গ্রহণযোগ্য নহে বিষয়টি মহোদয়ের সদয় অবগতি ও প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণের জন্য প্রেরণ করা হইল।”

Accordingly, we do not find any substance in the submissions of the learned advocate for the petitioner on this count. We are therefore, of the view that the wards were delimited having regard to so far as practicable, distribution of population save with a variation of not more than ten percent. It appears from the office record that after making enquiring and consideration of representations and suggestions of the Pourashava Chairman and other people of the Pourashava area Delimitation Officer by memo No. 98/566(500) dated 17-5-98 published a preliminary list of wards specifying the area making delimitation of 3 wards into 9 wards showing the number of wards, names of different mouzas, plot numbers and boundary of the wards with a notice inviting objections and suggestions from the people of the Pourashava area within 15 days from the date of publication of the said notice and endorsed copies of the said notification to the respondent Nos. 1, 3 and 4 the Chairman and all Commissioners of Lalmohan Pourashava, Office-bearers of different political parties, business organisations, local elites and we have noticed from the office record that these were received by them and the Chairman of Lalmohan Pourashava and other people of the locality filed objections and suggestions to the respondent No. 2. It appears from office record at page 112 that the respondent No. 2 by memo No. 670 dated 1-6-98 forwarded to the prescribed authority 12 (twelve) objections and suggestions with a concise statement of the objections to give its decision. From the office record we find that the respondent No. 4 by memo No. Poura-2/ward-6/98/769 dated 4-6-98 issued notice fixing 7-6-98 for hearing of objections/suggestions before the Joint Secretary, Md Maksumul Hoque and endorsed copies of these notices to the Deputy Commissioner and the Delimitation Officer for effecting service of the notice upon the persons who filed the said objections.
