Annexure-H (4) is the copy of the two Gazette notifications by which it was shown that in LA Case No. 63/1959-60 the unused land had been returned to the former owners of the land vide Gazette notification dated 29th November, 1993 and also in the Gazette notification dated 29 December, 1993 with regard to LA Case No. 63/1959-60 the unused lands were returned. Both were published in the Bangladesh Gazetee on 2nd December, 1993. In reply to the Ministry the Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA), Dhaka, informed the Government that in the relevant section of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA) no papers were available with regard to this acquisition of SA and CS Plot Nos. 24, 25, 26, 42 and 43 in the Samir Mouza. The land in question was under water at the relevant time and it was found that the suit land was under possession of the owners M Mohsin and others and this RAJUK did not take any step for returning the same to the owners. It was further replied that Plot Nos. 24, 25, 26, 42 and 43 of Samir Mouja was acquired by RAJUK vide LA Case No. 33/1958-59 and Gazette Notification was published on 23-6-60. It was also seen that the possession was taken by the RAJUK on 4-8-59 and 21-9-60. Further, it was reported that CS Plot Nos. 24, 25, 26, 42 and 43 of Samir Mouja and Plot No. 87 of Mohakhali Mouja were not acquired and the papers and documents of the aforesaid two moujas were not available in the LA Office. Further, it was stated from the office of the LA Collector that though the Gazette Notification dated 23-6-60 was published, no document was available with regard to taking over possession of the aforesaid plots by the requiring body. The lands in question were low lands and the same was under possession of the owners, namely, Mr Mohsin and others.

<u>6. In the affidavit-in-reply the petitioners have filed a letter dated 30th October, 1984 issued by the Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms. It was addressed to the Secretary, Ministry of Works. In this letter the Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms expressed their views that the lands which were purportedly acquired but not used by the requisitioning authority till today should be given back to the owners and the same cannot be kept unused for an indefinite period. The decision as well as the principles enunciated by the Government that if it is found that in spite of acquisition the land in question remained unused for indefinite period and for a long time the same should be released in favour of the owners even without referring the matter to the requiring body. On the basis of the aforesaid decision, of the Government a circular was issued on 22-5-86 by the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms. This circular is very important for the purpose of the present case. In the circular it was categorically stated that the purported acquired land, the possession of which has not yet been taken by the requiring body, should be returned to the owners. Even in the case of failing to pay the full compensation the Deputy Commissioner will also be authorised to take back those lands from the requiring body.</u>

7. Further, it was decided that in cases where the owners of the unused lands applied for getting back their lands, the Deputy Commissioner shall give a report on such lands and the same with comments the Deputy Commissioner should return to the Ministry for its consideration. The circular of the Government dated 22-5-86 is Annexure X(I). Annexure-X(2) is the rent receipt wherein the rent of the land in question was paid by Md Abdul Mannan for a sum of Taka 1,947.00. It was paid on 31-12-89. Annexure-X(2) also bears the name of Md Abdul Mannan. The mutation was made on 8-11-89 in respect of the suit land. Annexure-X(3) also shows payment of rent. Annexure-X series futher show several rent receipts and also mutation of the name of Md Shahjahan vide Mutation Case No. 406 dated 7-1-88. These rent receipts vide Annexure-X(4) series show payment of rent for the disputed lands for several other years and a duplicate carbon receipt is also annexed in the name of Mohsin Housing Commercial Complex which is a proprietorship business of M Mohsin Hossain, one of the petitioners before this Court. Another annexure shows the name of Mohsin Hossain mutated in the record of rights vide Mutation Case No. 1330/1989-90 dated 5-2-90. Annexure-X(5) series show that payment of rent by Mrs Masuma Khan with the DCR dated 6-2-90. The mutation was also made in the name of Mrs Masuma Khan vide Mutation Case No. 1331 of 1989-90 dated 5-2-90. Annexure-X(6) shows that the petitioners prayed to the District Adjutant of Ansar and VDP for giving whole-time guards for the petitioner''s property on the ground that some unauthorised persons were threatening to come over and illegally occupy the suit lands.

8. The petitioners also filed an application before the Officer-in-Charge of Gulshan Police Station for posting guards and on their prayer eight armed Ansars were posted in the suit lands in order to protect it from the hands of the tresspassers. Annexure-X(8) and X(9) show that the armed Ansars were posted there and their expenses would be borne by the land owners, namely, the petitioners. Annexure-X(10) is a copy of the Gulshan Model Town Master Plan in which the yellow area has been shown as vacant as the same had not been used by the DIT Mr Rafiqul Huq has produced before the Court a big master plan of Gushan Model Town from which he has shown the yellow colour marked area that the same still remained unused and outside the Model Town Plan though it was purportedly acquired in the year 1960.

9. In the affidavit-in-opposition as we have stated the case of respondent No. 4 is that since this was acquired in the year 1960 by Gazettee Notification, the present petitioners had no locus standi to claim the aforesaid lands and in that afidavit-in-opposition they have annexed a paper as Annexure-A showing the persons to whom the compensation has been given. But it appears that these persons are different from the predecessors-in-interest of the present petitioners. It was not denied that the predecessors-in-interest were the owners of the aforesaid lands, but the compensation had been given to some other persons excepting the predecessors-in-interest of the present petitioners.

10. Mr Rafiqul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that though on paper it was allegedly shown that the suit area was purported to have been acquired for the master plan of Gulshan Model Town, yet it was not, in fact, acted upon for last 37 years. It is his case that it was the provision of law that within two weeks from the date of requisition the possession should be taken over. But in the instant case for last 37 years possession was not taken over by the Government. He has further submitted that the petitioners have annexed so many papers and documents, as discussed above, in order to show their continuous possession of the suit property. On the other hand he submits that the respondents, particularly, respondent No. 4 failed to show by producing any documents before this Court that the possession was taken over by the RAJUK and they are maintaining the possession since 1960. It is submitted that only a Gazette Notification was shown that the land in question was acquired in 1960. Excepting that, with regard to the taking over possession and also with regard to payment of compensation, the respondents failed to produce any paper or document before this Court.

<u>11. In such a situation the learned Advocate submits that though allegedly it was acquired in 1960, yet for last 37 years such alleged acquisition was not acted upon and previously the predecessors of the present petitioners and after transfer the present petitioners have been continuously possessing the suit land. It is further strengthened by the fact that the petitioners have shown before this Court the master plan of the Gulshan Model Town and this map clearly shows that this suit area till today remains vacant and outside the Gulshan Model Town Master Plan. This Gulshan Master Plan has already been completed and there is no extension of the master plan as required by RAJUK under the Town Improvement Act. Since the possession of the suit property was and is still with the predecessors-in-interest of the petitioners and after transfer with the present petitioners for last 37 years and since it appears that the predecessors-in-interest of the petitioners were not given any compensation till today and since it was not included in the Gulshan Model Town Master Plan and there is no amendment of that plan by the RAJUK by Gazette Notification, we are of the view that the alleged acquisition was not acted upon and suit property still remained unused, as well as remained outside the master plan of the Gulshan Model Town. Further, it appears to us that the compensation had not been given to the predecessors-in-interest of the petitioners.</u>

<u>12. Mr Rafiqul Huq has drawn our attention to sections 73 and 74 of the Town Improvement Act wherein it is clearly provided that the master plan shall include the area in which the buildings and other things will be constructed and this master plan will be published in the official Gazette. The learned Advocate for the respondents, particularly, respondent No. 4 RAJUK failed to show any such Gazette Notification. Further, it appears that for alteration, amendment and extension of the master plan the Gazette Notification will be necessary. The master plan of Gulshan Model Town was produced before this Court which shows that the suit property was not included in the master plan of Gulshan Model Town and for last 37 years those remained unused outside the master plan. The learned Advocate for the RAJUK submits that .the RAJUK is taking steps for allotment of the aforesaid land. But he failed to produce before this Court any Gazette Notification which is required for amendment or alteration or extension of the master plan. Since the suit land in question still remains outside the master plan of Gulshan Model Town and, since for its extension there is no Gazette Notification, we find that there is clear violation of the provisions of sections 73 and 74 of the Town Improvemen Act. By violating the provisions of the aforesaid sections of TI Act the respondents RAJUK is not authorised to take possession of the land in question after 37 years without amending the master plan of Gulshan Model Town in accordance with law.</u>

<u>13. Mr Rafiqul Huq further submits that this Town Improvement Act was amended in the year 1987 by Act No. XXIX of 1987.In pursuance of the provision of section 79 of the Town Improvement Act, the provisions of the Acquisition and Requisition of the Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance No. II of 1982) will be applicable in the cases of RAJUK in respect of the properties acquired under the Town Improvement Act. Mr Huq further submits that since the Town Improvement Act was amended making this Ordinance II of 1982 applicable in the case of acquisition of the lands by RAJUK and since the possession of the suit land has not been taken over by the RAJUK and the compensation had not been given to the predecessors-in-interest of the petitioners, the proceeding is still continuing and, as such, at present the proceeding will be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Ordinance II of 1982. Mr Huq further submits that since this provisions of Ordinance II of 1982 have been made applicable in the case of acquisition under the Town Improvement Act, section 79 of the TI Act as amended has been attracted.</u>

14. Section 79(2) of the Town Improvement Act, as amended, runs as follows :

"79(2). The acquisition of any land or interest in land for the Kartripakkha under this section, or for any scheme under this Act, shall be deemed to be an acquisition for a public purpose within the meaning of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (II of 1982) and the provisions of the said Ordinance shall apply to all such proceedings".

<u>15. Mr Huq submits that since the provisions of the Ordinance II of 1982 are applicable and since it is admitted position that for last 37 years the suit lands remained unused for the purpose for which it was purportedly acquired, the Deputy Commissioner is bound to release the aforesaid lands in view of the fact that this Ordinance has been made applicable in the cases of the acquisition made by RAJUK, we find substance in the above submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners.</u>

<u>16. It is further submitted that the decision taken by the Government by the resolution of the inter-ministerial meeting in 1984 and the subsequent letters of the Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms and further the circular issued by the Government in 1986 as referred to above clearly show that the Government had taken decision in respect of all the acquired but unused lands in this country. The Government took a decision that if it is found that the lands purportedly acquired was not used for a long time for the said purpose they should be given back to the owners even without the consent or consulting the requiring body. The petitioners have annexed several documents to show that in pursuance of this decision of the Government as well as the circular issued subsequently several hundreds of unused lands which were purportedly acquired earlier were directed to be released in favour of the previous owners by issuing Gazette Notification. Mr Huq submits that since this is the policy/decision of the Government since 1984 and since this policy decision is applicable to all cases of the country with regard to unused lands though acquired earlier and since the decision of the Government had been acted upon in several case, such policy decision of the Government should also be applicable in the case of present petitioners in view of the fact that admittedly the suit lands remained unused for last 37 years though purportedly RAJUK acquired it for the master plan of Gulshan Model Town. Further, he submits that even the plan itself shows that the land in question remained outside the Gulshan Model Town Master Plan till today and there was no Gazette Notification in pursuance of sections 73 and 74 of the Town Improvement Act for amendment or further extension of the Gulshan Model Town Master Plan. Mr Huq submits that in the present case the general policy decision of the Government should also be applicable. We find force in the above contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioners. He further submits that taking advantage of law or by misreading the provision of law the authority cannot deprive the citizens of this country of their proprietary right.</u>

17. Mr Huq further submits that since this overall policy of the Government initiated from the year 1984 and since in the meantime it was acted upon and in several acquisition cases the unused lands were given back to the original owners, the petitioners should not be an exception of that. Mr Huq has further drawn our attention to Articles 27, 31 and 42 of the Constitution, namely, the fundamental rights of the citizens. Article 27 provides that all citizens are equal before law and are entitled to equal protection of law. Article 31 provides that to enjoy the protection of the law, and to be treated in accordance with law, and only in accordance with law, is the inalienable right of every citizen, wherever he may be, and of every other person for the time being within Bangladesh, and in particular no action detrimental to the life, liberty, body, reputation or property of any person shall be taken except in accordance with law. Article 42 provides that subject to any restrictions imposed by law, every citizen shall have the right to acquire, hold, transfer or otherwise dispose of property, and no property shall be compulsorily acquired , nationalised or requisitioned save by authority of law. Mr Huq submits that considering the above the Government had taken the overall policy of releasing the unused lands purportedly acquired earlier in favour of the owners.

18. He further submits that since policy of the Government had been acted upon and the unused land in several LA Cases had already been released in favour of the owners, the petitioners are entitled to get back their lands in view of the provisions of Article 27, 31 and 42 of the Constitution. We find force in the above submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners. Since taking advantage of certain law the authority had violated the rights of the present petitioners guaranteed under the Constitution as stated above and since the land in question though acquired kept unused for long 37 years, we are of the view that definitely such an action of the authority offended the fundamental rights, namely, Articles, 27, 31 and 42 of the Constitution. In this view of the matter, we find that the claim of the present petitioners should succeed.

<u>19. Mr Rafiqul Huq has referred before us the Administrative Law, International Student Edition, by HWR Wade and CF Forsyth, at 418 regarding Inconsistency and Unfairness Legitimate Expectation. He submits that the petitioners have got the legitimate expectation in view of the fact that in pursuance of the overall policy for giving back the unused acquired lands to the previous owners, every person in the country whose property was allegedly acquired but kept unused for such unusual longer period, can expect that his property should be returned to him otherwise there will be discrimination between citizen and citizen. It is provided in that book that : "Inconsistency of policy may also amount to an abuse of discretion, particularly, when undertaking or statement of intent are disregarded unfairly or contrary to citizen''s legitimate expectation. The Privy Council, in holding that the Government of Hong Kong must honour its public understanding to treat its deportation case on its merit, had applied the principles that a public authority is bound by its understanding."</u>

<u>"If the published policy was to be changed, the applicant should be given full and serious consideration whether there is some ever riding public interest justifying tiler new departure "Courts now expect the Government Departments to honour their statements of policy or intention or else to treat the citizen with the fullest personal consideration. Unfairness in the form of unreasonableness is clearly allied to unfairness by violation of natural justice. It was in the latter context that the doctrine of legitimate expectation was invented, but it is now providing to be a source of substantive as well as of procedural rights, Lord Scarman has stated emphatically that unfairness in the purported exercise of power can amount to an abuse or excess of power, and this may become an important general doctrine."</u>

<u>It was further stipulated :</u>

<u>"The argument under the label ''estoppel'' and the ''legitimate expectation'' arguments are substantially the same. In this conflict of doctrines the demands of fairness are proving the stronger. But those demands cannot be pressed to the point where they obstruct changes of policy which a Government should be at liberty to make within its discretionary powers, or legitimate practices such as selective prosecution of tax offenders by the Inland Revenue". It further provides that in the same way the Court of Appeal held that the public authority has a duty to act with fairness and consistency in its dealings with the public, and that if it makes inconsistent decisions unfairly or unjustly it misuses its powers.</u>

20. Mr Hasan Arif, the learned Advocate appearing for respondent No. 4, submits that since the notification of acquisition had been published in the year 1960, the matter became past and closed and it cannot be agitated anymore. It is difficult for us to accept the above contention in view of the fact that this Court has got the jurisdiction to see as to whether the acquisition proceeding has been legally implemented or not. We have already discussed above that it was purportedly acquired for Gulshan Model Town Master Plan, but this land in question was kept unused and outside the plan for last 37 years and this area was not included in the master plan of Gulshan Model Town. Further, we have already found that since the possession was not taken over and since the predecessors-in-interest of the petitioners as well as the petitioners have been continuously possessing the same and since the compensation has not been given to the predecessors-in-interest of the petitioners, acquisition in fact was not acted upon. Rather it appears to us that this was purportedly acquired for a different purpose which was not permitted by law. Further, we have already held that this acquisition was not completed in respect of the suit lands and that is why the provisions of Ordinance No. II of 1982 will be applicable. Mere Gazette Notification in the year 1960 is not enough unless and until the other provisions of law have been complied with. Since the compensation has not been given and since the owners are in possession although which has been proved by different papers and documents as discussed above, we are of the view that the submissions made by the learned Advocate for respondent No. 4 have got no substance.

21. Mr Hasan Arif further submits that the present petitioners have no locus standi to file this writ petition in view of the fact that they are not the original owners of the suit land and after acquisition the original owners had no legal right to transfer the same to the present petitioners. It is difficult for us to accept the above submission of Mr Hasan Arif in view of the fact that by registered transfer deeds the present petitioners have become the successors of the original owners and if the original owners are entitled to challenge this acquisition proceedings definitely the present petitioners being successors- in-interest have got the locus standi to challenge the acquisition in question. Since by the registered deeds the land in question was transferred to the present petitioners and since the names of the predecessors-in-interest of the petitioners were recorded in the record of the rights and since the names of the present petitioners were also mutated in the record of rights and since then they have been all along paying the rents to the Government in respect of the suit land, it shows that the predecessors-in-interest as well as the present petitioners have been continuing their possession in the suit property. Mr Hasan Arif has also raised some question in respect of the validity of the deeds in question. But this Court cannot go into the right and title of the predecessors-in-interest of the petitioners as well as the present petitioners in view of the fact that prima facie it shows that the predecessors- in-interest of the petitioners had transferred the suit lands to the present petitioners by registered instruments. As such, there is no scope for this Court to inquire and investigate into the allegation of Mr Hasan Arif. As such we find no substance in his contention. By transfer through valid registered deed, the petitioners stepped into the shoes of the original owners. Further, the title of the petitioners in the lands in question can only be challenged by the previous owners and nobody else.

22. Mr Hasan Arif further submits that the RAJUK has been taking steps for allotting as well as using the said property. Mr Rafiqul Huq submits that as back as from the year 1992 the present petitioners are trying to get the land released from the acquisition and they made several representations to different authorities for appropriate relief. Seeing the efforts of the present petitioners, now the RAJUK is claiming that they are taking steps to do something with regard to the suit property. Mr Huq submits that this is a malafide intention and they are trying to frustrate the purpose as well as the policy decision of the Government. Since it appears for us that the present petitioners have been possessing the suit land and since they are trying to get their land released from acquisition, it is difficult for us to hold that the RAJUK is doing something for extension of the master plan of Gulshan Model Town. As the lands in question are still under the possession of the petitioners and as there was no Gazette Notification showing the amendment for inclusion of the suit lands in question under the master plan of Gulshan Model Town, we are of the view that the claim of the learned Advocate for respondent No. 4 is absolutely baseless and it is now being made only to frustrate the purpose of the present petitioners case. In this view of the matter, we do not find substance in the submissions of Mr Hasan Arif.

23. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the legal position as well as the Government decision and policy as discussed above and also considering the papers and documents annexed with the Writ Petition and affidavit-in-reply as discussed above, we are of the view that this Writ Petition should succeed and the petitioners should get proper relief as prayed for.

24. In the result, this Rule is made absolute and let the petitioners continue their possession in the suit lands as they are continuing for last 37 years. The respondents are directed to release the suit lands, namely, SA Plot Nos. 24, 25, 26, 42 and 43 of Mouza Samir Police Station Tejgaon now Gulshan, District Dhaka measuring 4.79 acres of land from LA Case No. 33/1958-59 as unused lands in favour of the petitioners immediately.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, we pass no order as to cost.

End.

lawyer:
Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, with Abdul Kalam Azad, Advocates—For the Petitioner. 
Golam Arshad, Advocate—For Respondent Nos. 1-3. 
Mozammel Hossain with Harem-or-Rashid, Advocates —For Respondent No. 4.

full_judgment:
AFM Abdur Rahman J : By this Rule Nisi, dated 6-1-2008 the writ petitioner Md Habibur Rahman, challenged the legality and propriety of the judgment and order passed by the Administrator of Waqf on 6-9-2007 in connection with Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, having EC No. 8093, appointing the respondent No. 4 as mutwalli of the said Waqf Estate together with an advisory committee, rejecting the application for extension (renewal) of the period of the existing mutwalli committee, represented by the petitioner.

2. Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, having EC No. 8093, was created by Sheik Fakir Mahmud through a registered waqf deed being No. 810 dated 14-2-1940. As per the terms of the said waqf deed the sons and descendants of the waqif, who are pious and religious shall, by turn, be the mutwalli of the said waqf estate. The 3rd son of the waqif through the first wife, Hafez Moniruddin, was appointed as the first mutwalli of the said waqf estate. The waqf had two wives having each three sons. As per the terms of the deed after the death of the 1st mutwalli, Hafez Moniruddin, another descendent of the waqif named Tamizuddin was appointed as the second mutwalli of the waqf estate and after the demise of the second mutwalli, one Haji Ramizuddin Bhasani became the mutwalli. Meanwhile, one Abdul Maleq instituted Title Suit No. 178 of 1976, claiming title on the waqf property and the Administrator of Waqf, considering the circumstances, appointed a waqf, committee on 21-6-1995 for a term of two years under the presidentship of Haji Ramizuddin Bhasani and the other four persons from amongst the descendants of the waqif. The said mutwalli committee was extended for a further period of three years. But the legality of the said waqf committee was challenged by one Abdul Hossain before the Administrator of Waqf, who cancelled the said waqf committee by his order dated 17-11-1998 and appointed the said Abul Hossain as mutwalli of the waqf estate. This order of appointment of Abul Hossain as mutwalli was challenged by Haji Ramizuddin Bhasani in Writ Petition No. 3903 of 1998 and the Rule was made absolute through the judgment dated 24-5-1998 declaring the appointment of Abul Hossain as without lawful authority with further declaration that the waqf committee headed by Haji Ramizuddin Bhasani as lawful. The Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1292 of 1999 preferred by the Abul Hossain was dismissed on 6-3-2002. A further Review Petition No. 26 of 2002 was also dismissed. Later, the said Haji Ramizuddin Bhasani died on 16-1-2003 when the waqf committee was reconstituted with one of the descendents of the waqif Md Muslimuddin, son of Tamizuddin as chairman, who when died, the said committee was again reconstituted with the president ship of Haji Md Nabiullah. Thereafter, the tenure of the said committee was fixed for two years ending on 26-11-2006. Later, before the expiry of the tenure, the writ petitioner as the secretary of the said waqf committee, filed application before the Administrator of Waqf, respondent No. 2, praying for extension/renewal of the tenure of the waqf committee for five years and the same prayer was further renewed by another application filed on 21-1-2007. Thereafter, on 19-6-2005 one Nur Hossain, son of Abul Hossain, by filing application before the respondent No. 2, prayed for appointment as mutwalli of the said waqf estate and one Md Alamgir Siddique, the respondent No. 4, also filed application on 11-9-2006 praying for substitution of his name in place of Md Nur Hossain as the said Md Nur Hossain left for Italy. Thereafter, the Deputy Administrator of Waqf, respondent No. 3, took up the three sets of application for disposal and by the impugned order dated 6-9-2007 rejected the applications filed by the writ petitioner and allowed the application of Mr Md Alamgir Siddique, appointing him as mutwalli of the said waqf estate together with an advisory committee. By challenging the said judgment and order passed by the Deputy Administrator of Waqf-1, the petitioner obtained this Rule.

3. The Rule was opposed by the respondent No. 2, the Administrator of Waqf, and the respondent No. 4, Md Alamgir Siddique both of whom preferred affidavit-in-opposition.

4. It has been asserted in the affidavit-in-opposition that this Rule is liable to be discharged since the petitioner after having preferred a suit against the self same impugned order, lost the same and preferred an appeal under section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 before the District Judge, Dhaka and having lost the same, preferred a revisional application before the High Court Division which was dismissed as not being pressed and therefore, the instant Rule is a misconceived one. It has been further asserted that the Administrator of Waqf upon considering the circumstances, of the waqf estate, came to a lawful finding that all the parties involved in the waqf estate, being beneficiary of the same, should be allowed to participate in the Administration of the waqf estate and, as such, the Administrator of waqf appointed the grand son of the first wife, the respondent No. 4, as the mutwalli and also constituted an advisory committee with the other beneficiary of the waqf estate and, as such, no illegality or irreasonability was committed by the Administrator of Waqf.

5. It has been further asserted that it is the absolute domain of the Administrator of Waqf to renew any mutwalli committee as no right accrued to the mutwalli committee to have an extension or renewal of the same as of right, so far as the Waqf Ordinance 1962 is concerned. Therefore, the instant Rule is liable to be discharged.

6. In this Rule the learned Mr Senior Counsel, Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, appeared on behalf of the writ petitioner while the learned Advocate, Mr Golam Arshad, represented the respondent No. 2, the Administrator of Waqf. The learned Advocate, Mr Mahbubey Alam, appeared on behalf of the respondent No. 4, who having been appointed meanwhile as Attorney General of Bangladesh, the learned Advocate, Mr Md Harun-ur-Rashid, along with the learned Advocate, Mozammel Hossain, who argued on behalf of the respondent No. 4.

7. At the very outset of the hearing, while confronted with the query from this Court as to the maintainability of the instant writ petition in view of the impugned order passed under the Provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 which attracts appeal to the District Judge, the learned Senior Counsel, Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, admits that the instant appointment of the respondent No. 4, as mutwalli, is an appointment virtually under the Provision of section 43 and not under the Provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962, since, although the applications filed by one Mr Nur Hossain and substituted by the respondent No. '4 before the Administrator of Waqf on the allegation of committing irregularity and misappropriation of the waqf fund by the existing mutwalli committee, yet as the period of the mutwalli committee was expired and accordingly, the same was not in existence on the date of passing of the impugned order, the non-renewal of the period of earlier mutwalli committee cannot be treated as a removal of the mutwalli under the Provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962, rather the appointment of the respondent No. 4 as mutwalli must be treated as an appointment under the Provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962, since at that point of time there was no mutwalli or mutwalli committee existing in the said waqf estate.

8. The learned Senior Counsel, Mr Khondkar Mahbubuddin Ahmed, further admits that the petitioner preferred appeal against the impugned order before the District Judge, Dhaka as required under section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 and having lost there, the petitioner went to the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division, but his motion was ultimately rejected as being not pressed. Therefore, the learned Senior Counsel, Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, concedes to the legal aspect of the case that the instant writ petition is not maintainable.

9. But the learned Senior Counsel, Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, yet while taken this Court through the impugned order draws the attention of this Court to the illegality committed by the Administrator of Waqf in respect of appointing the respondent No. 4 for unlimited period and argues that the appointment of mutwalli under section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 must be for a limited period as it is the special power of the Waqf Administrator for appointment of mutwalli irrespective of the terms and condition, as embodied in the waqf deed. Therefore, the learned Senior Counsel contends that despite the non-maintainability of the instant writ petition, the merit of the case is in his favour, which the learned District Judge, Dhaka in the appeal, preferred by the writ petitioner, wrongly decided and rejected the same, taking the appointment of the respondent No. 4 as an appointment under the Provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962. The learned Senior Counsel prays for passing appropriate order by this Court.

10. On the other hand, the learned Advocate, Mr Golam Arshad, appearing on behalf of the Administrator of Waqf, while has taken this Court through the impugned judgment passed by the Waqf Administrator, strenuously argues, that the appointment of the respondent No. 4, as mutwalli of the Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, is an appointment under the Provision of section 43 the Waqf Ordinance 1962 and, as such, appeal lies against such order which the petitioner since filed before the District Judge, Dhaka and had lost the same, the petitioner preferred the revisional application before the High Court Division which was also rejected and, as such, this Rule on the self same cause is not sustainable and is liable to be discharged.

11. The learned Advocate, Mr Golam Arshad, further argues that the renewal of any tenure of mutwalli or mutwalli committee is in the absolute domain of the Administrator of Waqf, which cannot be claimed as a matter of right. Moreover the appointment of mutwalli under the Provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 cannot be said that it must be confined to a particular tenure, rather if it appears to the Administrator of waqf that no mutwalli was functioning in any waqf estate or appointment of mutwalli is barred by some reason or that the existing mutwalli became unsound in mind or could not function as mutwalli by any constraint the Administrator of Waqf can appoint any person as mutwalli of the said waqf estate and in that case the Administrator of Waqf is not bound to limit to tenure of the mutwalli. Therefore, the learned Advocate, Mr Golam Arshad argues, that no illegality was committed by the Administrator of Waqf through the impugned order.

12. None argued on behalf of the respondent No. 4.

13. We have perused the writ petition, the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition and other materials on record. We have also considered the arguments as advanced at the Bar.

14. To dispose of this writ petition within a short span of discussion, the question of the maintainability of this writ petition may be disposed of at first.

15. While the mutwalli committee of Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, Bara Maghbazar, Dhaka headed by one Md Nabiullah with the present petitioner as secretary, was functioning from 29-11-2004 for two years, the writ petition filed application for renewal of the tenure of the said mutwalli committee on 12-10-2006 which was well within the period of tenure of the mutwalli committee. But when the impugned order dated 6-9-2007 was passed, the tenure of the said mutwalli committee was expired, meaning thereby that at the time of taking decision in respect of the office of mutwalli of Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, neither there was any mutwalli nor any mutwalli committee functioning in the said waqf estate. It appears that two other applications were filed before the Administrator of Waqf alleging certain allegations against the mutwalli committee, functioning of which was also taken up by the Administrator of Waqf along with the application filed by the writ petitioner on 12-10-2006 and renewed by further application dated 21-1-2007. The Administrator of Waqf after perusing all the applications and considering the circumstances of the said Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, appointed respondent No. 4 as the mutwalli of the said waqf estate to be assisted by an advisory committee of five persons. Therefore, it is crystal clear, that this action of the Waqf Administration is not an action regarding removal of a mutwalli or mutwalli committee of an waqf estate and appointment of a new mutwalli for the same under the Provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962, rather this is an appointment of mutwalli under the Provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962. Section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 runs as follows

Waqf Ordinance, 1962.

Section 43—Power to appoint a Mutwalli in Certain Cases—In the case of any waqf of which there is no mutwalli or where there appears to the Administrator to be an impediment to the appointment of a mutwalli in terms of the deed of waqf or where the successor to the office of mutwalli is a minor, a person of unsound mind or a person adjudged insolvent by a competent Court of law, the Administrator may, for such period as he deems fit, appoint a person to act as mutwalli with notice to all the persons interested in the waqf. Any person aggrieved by such an appointment may, within three months from the date of the receipt of the notice, appeal to the District Judge; and the decision of the District Judge be final.

16. On the other hand, the Provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 involved a circumstance wherein an allegation against the mutwalli of a waqf estate was raised and upon such adjudication the mutwalli or the mutwalli committee is removed. The entire provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 is reproduced below;

Waqf Ordinance, 1962.

Section 32—Removal of Mutwalli in Certain Cases as his Liability for Breach of Trust (1)—Notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Ordinance or in any other law for the time being in force, the Administrator may, on his own motion or an application of any person, remove a mutwalli—

(i) for a breach of trust, mismanagement, malfeasance or misappropriation or

(ii) for any act of mutwalli causing loss of waqf property or affecting the proper administration, control of preservation of the waqf; or

(iii) if the mutwalli has been convicted more than once under section 61 or this Ordinance; or

(iv) If the existing mutwalli is found unsuitable, incompetent, negligent or otherwise undesirable: provided that no such order for removal of a mutwalli shall be made without giving him an opportunity of being heard.

(2) A mutwalli aggrieved by an order under sub-section (1) may within three months from the date of communication of such order, appeal to the District Judge against such order of removal, provided that no appeal shall lie against an order under sub-section (1) unless the mutwalli has made over charge of the waqf to the new mutwalli appointed under sub-section (4)

(3) A revision from every order passed in appeal by the District Judge under sub-section (2), if presented within ninety days from the date of such order, shall lie to the High Court, whose decision shall be final.

(4) When a mutwalli has been removed or when a mutwalli has resigned and his resignation has been accepted, the Administrator may appoint a new "mutwalli to whom the outgoing mutwalli shall make over possession and charge of management of the waqf property together with the case and all papers relating thereto by such date as may be specified by the Administrator.

(5) If an outgoing mutwalli fails or refuses to make over possession and charge of management of the waqf property together with the case and all papers relating thereto to the succeeding mutwalli under sub-section (4), the succeeding mutwalli or the Administrator may apply to the Deputy Commissioner who shall evict the outgoing mutwalli and make over possession of the waqf property together with the case and all papers relating thereto to the succeeding mutwalli or the Administrator, as the case may be.

(6) When a mutwalli commits a breach of trust or does any wrongful act causing loss to the waqf property, he shall be liable to make good the loss sustained by the waqf property or its beneficiaries.

17. Although the two other applications filed by the respondent No. 4 and one Nur Hossain raised allegations of misappropriation of fund and anomalies in the functioning of the mutwalli committee, yet while adjudication was made by the Administrator of Waqf on 6-9-2007 there was no mutwalli committee functioning or existing at that relevant point of time in the Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate. Therefore, under no chance the impugned order can be treated as passed under the Provision of section 32 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962, rather the same is an order passed under section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962.

18. Section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 provides for appeal before the District Judge. Since revision lies against the order of the District Judge under the Provision of section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, the petitioner correctly preferred the appeal before the District Judge, Dhaka, against the impugned order dated 6-9-2007 and then preferred a revisional application before the High Court Division against the dismissal of his appeal by the District Judge, Dhaka. But although the petitioner was liable to prefer civil petition for leave to appeal to the Appellate Division of the Bangladesh Supreme Court, instead he preferred the instant writ petition which is apparently erroneous. Therefore, this Court finds that this writ petition is not maintainable and accordingly, this Rule is liable to be discharged.

19. So far the merit of the case is concerned, the same although does not require any adjudication by this Court in view of the non-maintainability of the Rule, but as both the learned Advocate, Mr Golam Arshad and the learned Senior Counsel, Mr Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed argued on the point, this Court is inclined to shed some light on the merit of the case.

20. The learned Advocate, Mr Golam Arshad upon relying on the case of Haji Sharifuddin vs Administrator of Waqf passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 751 of 2006, strenuously argued that the claim of renewal of tenure of the mutwalli or mutwalli committee is not a matter of right and, as such, the impugned order is immune from any interference from this Court. In the referred case their Lordship in the Appellate Division held as under;

"It is on record that the writ-respondent No. 2, as a deserving candidate for the post of Mutwalli, was appointed in accordance with law. Since the period for which the petitioner was appointed has expired after the expiry of his tenure of office of mutwalli, he could not cling to the post as a matter of right."

<u>21. In view of the above decision, this Court finds that the writ petitioner although submitted an application before the Administrator of Waqf on 12-10-2006 renewed by another application dated 21-1-2007, with a prayer for renewal of the period of the mutwalli committee, the Administrator of Waqf rightly denied to concede to the prayer as the renewal is not a matter of right of the mutwalli or mutwalli committee, who is being appointed in exercise of discretionary power of the Waqf Administration under the Provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962.</u>

<u>22. But so far the question of appointment of the respondent No. 4 is concerned, this Court finds that the Administrator of Waqf appointed the respondent No. 4 for unlimited period which appears to be an illegality in view of the provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962.</u>

<u>23. It appears that the Provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 is a Provision for filling the stopgap in a waqf estate wherein by some reason mutwalli can be appointed in a waqf estate and therefore any appointment made under the Provision of section 43 of the Waqf Ordinance 1962 must be made for a limited period till the reason for stopgap is over. Therefore, the Administrator of Waqf while appointed the respondent No. 4 as a mutwalli of Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate ought to have fixed a period and since the period has not been fixed, the same can be fixed by the Administrator of Waqf after the disposal of this Rule, if the respondent No. 4 is otherwise competent to be the mutwalli of the waqf estate named Fakir Mahmud Waqf Estate, having EC No. 8093.</u>

<u>24. In view of the discussion and reasoning as above, this Court finds no merit in this Rule which is liable to be discharged.</u>

25. In the result, the Rule is discharged.

However, there shall be no order as to costs.

End.
